He would finish the day with 344 passing yards and 2 touchdowns, as Indianapolis defeated the [[Cincinnati Bengals|Bengals]], 27–0.{{Cite news |last=Keefer |first=Zack |date=October 19, 2014 |title=Colts' D is dominant in shutout win over Bengals |url=http://www.indystar.com/story/sports/nfl/colts/2014/10/19/colts-d-dominant-victory-cincinnati/17576265/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190906120320/https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/nfl/colts/2014/10/19/colts-d-dominant-victory-cincinnati/17576265/ |archive-date=September 6, 2019 |access-date=October 19, 2014 |work=[[The Indianapolis Star|Indy Star]]}} The shutout victory was the first for Indianapolis since a 23–0 win over the [[Tennessee Titans]] in December 2008.{{Cite web |last=Chappell |first=Mike |date=October 19, 2014 |title=Four-Down Territory: Colts shutout Bengals |url=http://www.theindychannel.com/sports/colts/four-down-territory-colts-shutout-bengals |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141021122734/http://www.theindychannel.com/sports/colts/four-down-territory-colts-shutout-bengals |archive-date=October 21, 2014 |access-date=October 19, 2014 |website=theindychannel.com}} Luck broke his single-season touchdown mark in the Colts Week 9 game against the [[2014 New York Giants season|New York Giants]], throwing four to bring his total to 26. He also became the first quarterback in 2014 to reach 3,000 passing yards.{{Cite news |last=Higham |first=Paul |date=November 4, 2014 |title=NFL: Andrew Luck throws four touchdowns as Indianapolis Colts beat New York Giants |url=http://www1.skysports.com/american-football/news/12040/9548998/nfl-andrew-luck-throws-four-touchdowns-as-indianapolis-colts-beat-new-york-giants |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141104234935/http://www1.skysports.com/american-football/news/12040/9548998/nfl-andrew-luck-throws-four-touchdowns-as-indianapolis-colts-beat-new-york-giants |archive-date=November 4, 2014 |access-date=November 4, 2014 |publisher=[[Sky Sports]]}} In Week 13, Luck threw a career-high 5 touchdown passes in a 49–27 win over the [[2014 Washington Redskins season|Washington Redskins]].{{Cite web |title=Washington Redskins at Indianapolis Colts – November 30th, 2014 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201411300clt.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171230061803/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201411300clt.htm |archive-date=December 30, 2017 |access-date=January 13, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} In addition, he also became the first quarterback to reach 4,000 passing yards in 2014. On December 4, Luck was named the AFC Offensive Player of the Month for November. In the month, Luck passed for 1,280 yards, 12 touchdowns, and had a quarterback rating of 112.0.{{Cite web |date=December 4, 2014 |title=Indianapolis Colts QB-Andrew Luck Named AFC Offensive Player of the Month for November |url=https://www.colts.com/video/colts-qb-andrew-luck-named-afc-offensive-player-of-the-month-for-november |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220202163827/https://www.colts.com/video/colts-qb-andrew-luck-named-afc-offensive-player-of-the-month-for-november |archive-date=February 2, 2022 |access-date=February 2, 2022 |website=Colts.com}} Entering a Week 14 matchup with the [[2014 Cleveland Browns season|Cleveland Browns]], Luck needed only 81 yards to surpass Peyton Manning for the most passing yards by a quarterback in their first 3 seasons.{{Cite web |date=December 7, 2014 |title=Andrew Luck rallies Colts past Browns with game-winning drive |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=400554422 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220202163828/https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=400554422 |archive-date=February 2, 2022 |access-date=February 2, 2022 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}} Luck passed for 294 yards to take the record, and engineered a fourth-quarter comeback by throwing a 1-yard touchdown pass to T. Y. Hilton to win the game 25–24.{{Cite web |date=December 7, 2014 |title=Andrew Luck rebounds, Colts edge Browns, 25–24 |url=http://www.nydailynews.com/sports/football/andrew-luck-rebounds-colts-edge-browns-25-24-article-1.2037047 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141222034119/http://www.nydailynews.com/sports/football/andrew-luck-rebounds-colts-edge-browns-25-24-article-1.2037047 |archive-date=December 22, 2014 |access-date=December 7, 2014 |website=nydailynews.com |agency=Associated Press}} After a Week 15 win against the Texans, Luck successfully led the Colts to the playoffs for the third straight year.{{Cite news |last=Wells |first=Mike |date=December 14, 2014 |title=Colts' Andrew Luck is 3-for-3 in making the playoffs |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/nflnation/post/_/id/153955/andrew-luck-is-3-for-3-in-making-the-playoffs |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220202163831/https://www.espn.com/blog/nflnation/post/_/id/153955/andrew-luck-is-3-for-3-in-making-the-playoffs |archive-date=February 2, 2022 |access-date=February 2, 2022 |work=[[ESPN.com]]}} Along with the division title, Luck also earned his third straight Pro Bowl berth.{{Cite web |last=Wells |first=Mike |date=December 23, 2014 |title=2015 Pro Bowl: Andrew Luck leads group of five Indianapolis Colts |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/nflnation/post/_/id/155666/2015-pro-bowl-andrew-luck-leads-group-of-five-indianapolis-colts |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220202163830/https://www.espn.com/blog/nflnation/post/_/id/155666/2015-pro-bowl-andrew-luck-leads-group-of-five-indianapolis-colts |archive-date=February 2, 2022 |access-date=February 2, 2022 |website=ESPN.com}} In Week 17, Luck broke Peyton Manning's franchise record for passing yards in a single-season. What a year he's had! #INDvsTEN |date=December 28, 2014 |access-date=February 2, 2022}} In the Colts' [[2014–15 NFL playoffs#AFC: Indianapolis Colts 26, Cincinnati Bengals 10|Wild Card Round]] game Football Reference]] |language=en}} === 2015 season === [[File:AndrewLuck camp2015 1.jpg|thumb|120px|left|Luck in 2015 at training camp]] On April 9, the Colts announced they had picked up the fifth-year option on Luck's contract, paying him a guaranteed $16.55 million in 2016. In Weeks 4 and 5, Luck missed the first two games of his career with an injured shoulder. Backup [[Matt Hasselbeck]] played in his place and led the team to a 16–13 overtime win over the [[2015 Jacksonville Jaguars season|Jacksonville Jaguars]], followed by a 27–20 ''Thursday Night Football'' victory over the [[2015 Houston Texans season|Houston Texans]].{{Cite web |last=Orr |first=Conor |date=April 9, 2015 |title=Colts pick up fifth-year option on Andrew Luck It's not the healthiest way to live."|source= –Andrew Luck{{Cite magazine |last=Borba |first=Kevin |date=December 6, 2022 |title=Andrew Luck opens up about what led to him retiring from the NFL |url=https://www.si.com/college/stanford/nfl/andrew-luck-opens-up-about-what-led-to-him-retiring-from-the-nfl |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221208025059/https://www.si.com/college/stanford/nfl/andrew-luck-opens-up-about-what-led-to-him-retiring-from-the-nfl |archive-date=December 8, 2022 |access-date=December 8, 2022 |magazine=Sports Illustrated}}}} [[File:Indianapolis Colts Town Hall May 2019 Andrew Luck 1.jpg|thumb|Luck speaking at a Colts fan event in May 2019.]] On August 24, 2019, after seven seasons and at the age of 29, Luck announced his retirement two weeks before the start of the season. At a press conference, he cited his recurrent cycle of injuries and rehabilitation as the primary reason,{{Cite web |last=Schwartz |first=Geoff |date=August 26, 2019 |title=I understand why Andrew Luck retired, because I've been in his shoes: Retired NFL lineman Geoff Schwartz describes just how awful it feels to go through the rigors of constant rehab |url=https://www.sbnation.com/nfl/2019/8/26/20832198/why-andrew-luck-retired-rehab-injuries |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220930225207/https://www.sbnation.com/nfl/2019/8/26/20832198/why-andrew-luck-retired-rehab-injuries |archive-date=September 30, 2022 |access-date=January 30, 2020 |website=SB Nation}} saying:
I've been stuck in this process. I haven't been able to live the life I want to live. It's taken the joy out of this game. The only way forward for me is to remove myself from football. This is not an easy decision. It's the hardest decision of my life. But it is the right decision for me.{{Cite web |last=Wells |first=Mike |date=24 August 2019 |title=Luck retires, calls decision 'hardest of my life' |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/27456682/luck-retires-calls-decision-hardest-my-life |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220930225210/https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/27456682/luck-retires-calls-decision-hardest-my-life |archive-date=September 30, 2022 |access-date=August 24, 2019 |website=ESPN.com}}
Due to retiring at the age of 29, Luck is considered by some to be among the best professional athletes to end their career during their prime.{{Cite web |last=DeArdo |first=Bryan |date=August 26, 2019 |title=NFL stars who retired early: Andrew Luck joins list of 10 other great players who stepped away in their prime |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/nfl-stars-who-retired-early-andrew-luck-joins-list-of-10-other-great-players-who-stepped-away-in-their-prime/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190827060211/https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/nfl-stars-who-retired-early-andrew-luck-joins-list-of-10-other-great-players-who-stepped-away-in-their-prime/ |archive-date=August 27, 2019 |access-date=August 28, 2019 |website=[[CBS Sports]]}}{{Cite web |last=Baker |first=Katie |date=August 26, 2019 |title=Andrew Luck and the Afterburn of Early Retirement |url=https://www.theringer.com/nfl/2019/8/26/20832885/andrew-luck-indianapolis-colts-early-athlete-retirements |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190827040155/https://www.theringer.com/nfl/2019/8/26/20832885/andrew-luck-indianapolis-colts-early-athlete-retirements |archive-date=August 27, 2019 |access-date=August 28, 2019 |website=[[The Ringer (website)|The Ringer]]}} After very few public appearances and no interviews following his retirement, an [[ESPN]] article written by [[Seth Wickersham]] in December 2022 went into more detail about Luck's decision. Luck clarified that while injuries played a role, another factor was a desire to save his relationship with his wife, Nicole. According to Luck, the development required to become a top tier NFL caliber quarterback caused friction with Nicole. manager of [[Stanford Cardinal football]] in November 2024.{{Cite news |last=Thamel |first=Pete |author-link=Pete Thamel |date=November 30, 2024 |title=Andrew Luck as Stanford's GM? What it means for the Cardinal and college football |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/42698084/andrew-luck-stanford-gm-means-cardinal-college-football |access-date=January 21, 2025 |work=[[ESPN]] |publisher=}} As one of his first acts as GM, Luck fired head football coach [[Troy Taylor (American football)|Troy Taylor]] on March 25, 2025, after two investigations into the latter's conduct towards female staffers.{{Cite web |last=Jeyarajah |first=Shehan |date=March 25, 2025 |title=Andrew Luck makes decision to fire Stanford coach Troy Taylor after reports Taylor mistreated female staffers |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-football/news/andrew-luck-makes-decision-to-fire-stanford-coach-troy-taylor-after-reports-taylor-mistreated-female-staffers/ |access-date=March 25, 2025 |website=[[CBS Sports]] |language=en}}{{Cite news |last1=Kamrani |first1=Christopher |last2=Mandel |first2=Stewart |author-link2=Stewart Mandel |date=March 25, 2025 |title=Stanford GM Andrew Luck fires football coach Troy Taylor following bullying investigations |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6219705/2025/03/25/stanford-fires-troy-taylor-andrew-luck/ |access-date=March 26, 2025 |work=[[The Athletic]] |publisher=[[The New York Times]] |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}} Luck then brought in [[Frank Reich]], who had coached him in Indianapolis in his final year in the NFL, to replace Taylor as Stanford's new coach on an interim basis.{{Cite web |last=Dubow |first=Josh |date=April 1, 2025 |title=Stanford introduces Frank Reich as interim football coach |url=https://www.nbcbayarea.com/news/sports/stanford-introduces-frank-reich-interim-football-coach/3833108/ |access-date=April 9, 2025 |website=NBC Bay Area |language=en-US}} The Cardinal went 4–8 in Luck's first full season as general manager, during which his focus was on developing the program for the long term and searching for a permanent head coach. Assistant nickels coach | highlights = * First-team All-[[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] ([[2010 All-Big 12 Conference football team|2010]]) | statlabel1 = [[Tackle (football move)|Total tackles]] | statvalue1 = 149 | statlabel2 = [[Quarterback sacks|Sacks]] | statvalue2 = 2.0 | statlabel3 = [[Fumble|Forced fumbles]] | statvalue3 = 1 | statlabel4 = [[Fumble|Fumble recoveries]] | statvalue4 = 1 | statlabel5 = [[Touchdown|Defensive touchdowns]] | statvalue5 = 1 | pfr = GachAn00 }} '''Andrew Gachkar''' (born November 4, 1988) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[San Diego Chargers]], [[Dallas Cowboys]], and [[Carolina Panthers]]. He was selected by the Chargers in the seventh round of the [[2011 NFL draft]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Missouri Tigers football|Missouri Tigers]]. He is currently the assistant nickels coach at [[Vanderbilt Commodores football|Vanderbilt]]. ==Early life== Gachkar grew up in [[Overland Park, Kansas]], and attended [[Blue Valley West High School]]. As a junior, he registered 83 tackles, 5 sacks, 2 interceptions (one returned for a [[touchdown]]) and 2 forced fumbles. As a senior, he was limited by a shoulder injury, but still managed to be a two-way player at [[running back]] and [[linebacker]]. He was rated the number 10 overall prospect in the state of [[Kansas]] by Super Prep. ==College career== Gachkar accepted a football scholarship from the [[University of Missouri]]. As a true freshman, he appeared in 14 games, playing mainly on special teams. He made 16 defensive tackles and one forced fumble. As a sophomore, he recovered from four surgeries in the off-season, where he had a rib removed to alleviate blood clotting issues in his right arm and upper body. He appeared in 14 games as a backup, collecting 28 tackles (one for loss). As a junior, he started in 13 games at [[strongside linebacker]], posting 80 tackles (second on the team), 3 sacks and 3 fumble recoveries (led the team). He was part of a defense that ranked 26th in the nation against the run (118.62-yard avg.). He had 4 tackles, one tackle, one forced fumble and 2 fumble recoveries against [[Nebraska Cornhuskers football|Nebraska]]. He made 9 tackles against [[Oklahoma State University]]. He had 10 tackles against [[Kansas State University]]. As a senior, he was moved to [[weakside linebacker]] to replace [[All-American]] [[Sean Weatherspoon]]. He started in 13 games, finishing with 51 tackles (led the team), 8.5 tackles for loss, one sack and 2 interceptions.{{cite web | title=Chargers draft Andrew Gachkar of Blue Valley West and Missouri in seventh round | website=Wichita Eagle | date=2011-04-30 | url=https://www.kansas.com/latest-news/article1062849.html | access-date=2025-05-18}} He was a part of the number one scoring defense in the nation. ==Professional career== ===San Diego Chargers=== Gachkar was selected by the [[San Diego Chargers]] in the seventh round (234th overall) of the [[2011 NFL draft]].{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2011/draft.htm |title=2011 NFL Draft Listing |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |access-date=March 15, 2020}} On July 28, 2011, he was signed to a four-year deal with the Chargers. As a rookie, he posted 15 defensive tackles and 12 [[special teams]] tackles (second on the team). He became a valuable [[special teams]] player, while also being a solid reserve [[linebacker]]. In 2012, he recorded 13 tackles (2 for loss), one sack and 8 [[special teams]] tackles. In 2013, he started 3 out of 16 games, making 33 tackles (one for loss), one forced fumble and 8 [[special teams]] tackles. He had 6 tackles and one forced fumble against the [[Tennessee Titans]]. He made 8 tackles against the [[Washington Redskins]]. In 2014, he received more playing time due to injuries and [[defensive coordinator]] [[John Pagano]] rotations at linebacker. He appeared in 15 games with 5 starts, registering, 49 tackles (6 for loss), one sack, one pass defensed 16 special teams tackles and also scored his first [[NFL]] touchdown against the [[St. Louis Rams]] on a fumble recovery. He had 8 tackles against the [[Denver Broncos]]. ===Dallas Cowboys=== On March 15, 2015, he signed with the [[Dallas Cowboys]] a two-year, $5.5 million contract, reuniting with former Chargers [[special teams]] coordinator [[Rich Bisaccia]].{{cite web|work=NFL.com|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/dallas-cowboys-land-linebacker-andrew-gachkar-0ap3000000479114|title=Dallas Cowboys land linebacker Andrew Gachkar|first=Marc|last=Sessler|date=March 15, 2015|accessdate=March 15, 2020}} As a reserve linebacker, he showed the ability to play all three positions and made [[Jasper Brinkley]] expendable.{{cite web| url=https://www.espn.com/blog/dallas-cowboys/post/_/id/4744785/cowboys-turn-attention-to-andrew-gachkar-at-middle-linebacker | title=Cowboys turn attention to Andrew Gachkar at middle linebacker | accessdate=March 15, 2020}} He started against the [[New Orleans Saints]] and posted 6 tackles. In the eighth game of the season against the [[Philadelphia Eagles]], he saw extended time in place of [[Sean Lee]] who was out with a concussion, while tallying 4 tackles (one for loss). He played in every game, registering 8 special teams tackles (tied for fourth on the team) and 13 defensive tackles. In 2016, he remained a core [[special teams]] player, making 7 defensive tackles, 2 quarterback pressures and 7 [[special teams]] tackles (tied for fourth on the team). In the season finale against the Eagles, the Cowboys rested players for the playoffs and Gachkar saw extended playing time, posting 5 tackles (one for loss), 2 quarterback pressures and a half-sack. He wasn't re-signed after the season.{{cite web| url=https://www.dallascowboys.com/news/free-agent-overview-gachkar-played-special-teams-versatile-lb-role-again-427541 | title=Free Agent Overview: Gachkar Played Special Teams, Versatile LB Role Again |access-date=July 11, 2020}} ===Jacksonville Jaguars=== On August 13, 2017, Gachkar signed with the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]].{{cite web|title=Jaguars Sign Linebacker Andrew Gachkar|url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/jaguars-sign-linebacker-andrew-gachkar-19183963|author=Oehser, John|website=Jaguars.com|date=August 13, 2017|access-date=July 11, 2020}} He was released by Jacksonville on September 2.{{cite web|title=Jaguars reduce active roster to 53 players|url=http://www.jaguars.com/news/article-JaguarsNews/Jaguars-reduce-active-roster-to-53-players/11928d4a-71bb-4c27-af08-70f67c3242e8|author=Oehser, John|website=Jaguars.com|date=September 2, 2017|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170905032258/http://www.jaguars.com/news/article-JaguarsNews/Jaguars-reduce-active-roster-to-53-players/11928d4a-71bb-4c27-af08-70f67c3242e8|archivedate=September 5, 2017|access-date=July 11, 2020}} ===Carolina Panthers=== On October 17, 2017, Gachkar signed with the [[Carolina Panthers]].{{cite web|title=Panthers sign LB Andrew Gachkar, waive QB Brad Kaaya|url=http://www.panthers.com/news/article-2/Panthers-sign-LB-Andrew-Gachkar-waive-QB-Brad-Kaaya/82760890-fb40-4877-87aa-4767971f0a6a|author=Henson, Max|website=Panthers.com|date=October 17, 2017|access-date=March 15, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171017202645/http://www.panthers.com/news/article-2/Panthers-sign-LB-Andrew-Gachkar-waive-QB-Brad-Kaaya/82760890-fb40-4877-87aa-4767971f0a6a|archive-date=October 17, 2017|url-status=dead|df=mdy-all}} He appeared in six games and was declared inactive in four contests, while making five [[special teams]] tackles (tied for third on the team). '''Andre Phillip Smith''' (born September 26, 1988) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[tight end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[Chicago Bears]], [[Dallas Cowboys]] and [[Cleveland Browns]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Virginia Tech Hokies football|Virginia Tech Hokies]].

==Early life==
Smith attended [[Seneca Valley High School]].<ref>{{cite web| url=https://patch.com/maryland/gaithersburg/graduate-on-verge-of-making-svhs-history | title=Graduate On Verge of Making SVHS History | date=27 April 2011 | accessdate=January 12, 2019}}</ref> He did not play organized football until his freshman season. He was a two-way player at [[tight end]], [[defensive end]] and [[linebacker]].

As a senior, he registered 18 receptions for 278 yards, 6 [[touchdown]]s, 44 tackles and 5 sacks. He received All-league and second-team All-state honors.

==College career==
Smith accepted a football scholarship from [[Virginia Tech]]. As a sophomore, he had 10 receptions (sixth on the team) for 129 yards and one [[touchdown]].

As a senior, he was known as a blocking [[tight end]], but was still able to start 12 out of 14 games, while posting 20 receptions (fourth on the team) for 195 yards and 5 [[touchdown]]s. He finished his college career with 25 starts out of 54 games, 39 receptions for 438 yards and 7 [[touchdown]]s.

==Professional career==
===Chicago Bears===
Smith was signed as an [[undrafted free agent]] by the [[Chicago Bears]] after the [[2011 NFL draft]] on July 26. On September 3, he was waived and signed to the [[practice squad]] the next day. On November 9, he was promoted to the active roster. He was declared inactive for the final 8 games.<ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.espn.com/blog/chicago/bears/post/_/id/4675135/offseason-position-outlook-tight-end | title=Offseason position outlook: Tight end | date=9 February 2012 | accessdate=January 12, 2019}}</ref> He was released on May 14, [[2012 NFL season|2012]].

===Indianapolis Colts===
On May 15, [[2012 NFL season|2012]], he was claimed off waivers by the [[Indianapolis Colts]]. He was released on August 31.

===Dallas Cowboys===
On December 11, [[2012 NFL season|2012]], he was signed by the [[Dallas Cowboys]] to their [[practice squad]].<ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.espn.com/blog/dallas/cowboys/post/_/id/4702983/cowboys-claim-cb-michael-coe | title=Cowboys claim CB Michael Coe | date=11 December 2012 | accessdate=January 12, 2019}}</ref>

In [[2013 NFL season|2013]], he played well enough in the preseason to force the team to make the unusual of move of keeping four [[tight end]]s.<ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.espn.com/blog/dallas-cowboys/post/_/id/4714049/andre-smith-not-relieved-just-yet | title=Andre Smith not relieved just yet | date=3 September 2013 | accessdate=January 12, 2019}}</ref> He appeared in 2 games and was declared inactive for 8 contests. His only statistic was the recovery of a [[squib kick]] that he returned for 10 yards. He was released on November 25.

===Cleveland Browns===
On November 26, [[2013 NFL season|2013]], he was claimed off waivers by the [[Cleveland Browns]].<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.cleveland.com/browns/index.ssf/2013/11/cleveland_browns_acquire_tight.html | title=Cleveland Browns acquire tight end Andre Smith off waivers from the Dallas Cowboys | date=27 November 2013 | accessdate=January 12, 2019}}</ref> He was released on May 19, [[2014 NFL season|2014]].

==Personal life==
Smith lost his mother during his senior year in high school. In 2017, he graduated from the [[police academy]] and started working for the Montgomery County Police Department.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.germantownpulse.net/single-post/2018/11/30/Coming-Home-for-Good-Former-NFL-Player-Now-Patrols-His-Hometown-Streets-in-Germantown-with-MCPD | title=Coming Home for Good: Former NFL Player Now Patrols His Hometown Streets with MCPD | accessdate=January 12, 2019}}</ref>

'''Andre Benoise Young''' (born November 22, 1960) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive back]] for two seasons for the [[San Diego Chargers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Louisiana Tech Bulldogs football|Louisiana Tech Bulldogs]].<ref>[https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/Y/YounAn20.htm Andre Young NFL & AFL Football Statistics - Pro-Football-Reference.com]</ref>

==Early life==
While in middle school, Young played as a [[quarterback]].<ref name="pro1">{{cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/633593747/?clipping_id=130611366|title=San Diego's Strong Safety Makes His First Pro Journey to End Zone (II)|work=[[Los Angeles Times]]|first=Dave|last=Distel|date=October 10, 1983|access-date=August 24, 2023|page=S12|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref> He attended [[West Monroe High School]] in [[West Monroe, Louisiana]], where he played [[offensive tackle]] and some [[tight end]] on the football team.<ref name=pro1/>

==College career==
As a freshman at [[Louisiana Tech University]], Young played [[weakside linebacker]] for the [[Louisiana Tech Bulldogs football|Bulldogs]].<ref name=pro1/> He earned first-team all-[[Southland Conference]] honors as a sophomore in 1979 at [[defensive end]].<ref name="who">{{cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/601187417/?clipping_id=130596947|title=Who's this Young man in San Diego's lineup?|work=[[Shreveport Journal]]|first=John James|last=Marshall|date=August 23, 1982|access-date=August 24, 2023|page=1C|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/539647200/?clipping_id=130597044|title=Southland Announces All-League Choices|work=[[The Daily Advertiser (Lafayette, Louisiana)|The Daily Advertiser]]|date=December 2, 1979|access-date=August 24, 2023|page=70|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref> Young was moved to [[middle linebacker]] the following season and again earned a first-team all-conference selection.<ref name=who/><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/537831078/?clipping_id=130597825|title=On All-SLC Squad: Four Cagers Selected|work=[[The Daily Advertiser (Lafayette, Louisiana)|The Daily Advertiser]]|date=November 30, 1980|access-date=August 24, 2023|page=72|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref> He changed positions once again as a senior; he was converted to a [[defensive back]].<ref name=who/>

==Professional career==
Young was selected in the tenth round (273rd overall) by the [[San Diego Chargers]] in the [[1982 NFL draft]].<ref name=who/> He started the preseason as the fifth-string [[strong safety]].<ref name=who/> In an exhibition against the [[Dallas Cowboys]], Young recorded four tackles, three assists, an interception, and a touchdown-saving pass deflection in two quarters of playing time.<ref name=who/> He earned a spot on the Chargers' final roster.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/600433009/?clipping_id=130602526|title=Bennett cut by Bengals|work=[[Shreveport Journal]]|date=September 8, 1982|access-date=August 24, 2023|page=3C|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref> In his NFL debut, Young forced a fumble, recovered two fumbles, and intercepted a pass from [[Craig Morton]] in their season-opening win over the [[Denver Broncos]], with the ''[[Los Angeles Times]]'' saying that "there couldn't have been a more unlikely defensive star."<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/389268898/?clipping_id=130601893|title=Here's a Big Switch: Chargers' Defense Crushes Broncos|work=[[Los Angeles Times]]|first=Chris|last=Cobbs|date=September 12, 1982|access-date=August 24, 2023|page=S1|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref>

On October 9, 1983, Young picked off [[Jim Zorn]] and returned it 40 yards for a touchdown to help the Chargers beat the [[Seattle Seahawks]] 28–21.<ref name="pro">{{cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/633593719/?match=1&clipping_id=101501544|title=San Diego's Strong Safety Makes His First Pro Journey to End Zone (I)|work=[[Los Angeles Times]]|first=Dave|last=Distel|date=October 10, 1983|access-date=August 24, 2023|page=S1|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref> It was both his first touchdown as a pro, and his first since high school.<ref name=pro/> In the 1984 season opener, Young recorded two interceptions to help the Chargers defeat the [[Minnesota Vikings]], 42–13.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/400999646/?clipping_id=130612129|title=Marine Tactics Can't Stop Chargers, 42-13 (II)|work=[[Los Angeles Times]]|first=Chris|last=Cobbs|date=September 3, 1984|access-date=August 24, 2023|page=S10|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref> He was waived by the Chargers on July 9, 1985.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/569798741/?match=1&clipping_id=130613177|title=Chargers waive goodbye to veterans|work=[[Escondido Times-Advocate]]|first=Jay|last=Posner|date=July 10, 1985|access-date=August 24, 2023|page=D1|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref>

'''Andrew DePaola Jr.''' ({{respell|dee|PAW|lə}}; born July 28, 1987) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[long snapper]] for the [[Minnesota Vikings]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He made his NFL debut with the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] on September 7, 2014.<ref name="Andrew DePaola">{{cite web|url=http://www.buccaneers.com/team-and-stats/roster/Andrew-DePaola/8a7d21ff-2dda-4407-960c-bc2d23ac9b14|title=Andrew DePaola|access-date=December 9, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150202081423/http://www.buccaneers.com/team-and-stats/roster/Andrew-DePaola/8a7d21ff-2dda-4407-960c-bc2d23ac9b14|archive-date=February 2, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> He played football and [[baseball]] in high school before playing [[college football]] for the [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights football|Rutgers Scarlet Knights]]. He has also played in the NFL for the [[Chicago Bears]], [[Oakland Raiders]], and [[Carolina Panthers]].

==Early life and college==
DePaola was born in [[Sparks, Maryland]], a town in Baltimore County.<ref name="NFL">{{cite web|url=http://www.nfl.com/player/andrewdepaola/2538247/profile|title=Andrew DePaola|publisher=NFL|access-date=December 9, 2014}}</ref> In 2001, DePaola entered [[Hereford High School (Parkton, Maryland)|Hereford High School]] in [[Parkton, Maryland]], as a freshman with a passion for baseball, but soon shifted his focus to football.<ref name="Hereford Harbringer">{{cite web|url=http://issuu.com/herefordharbinger/docs/final_full_paper|title=Andrew DePaola|date=November 6, 2013 |publisher=Hereford High School|access-date=December 9, 2014}}</ref> DePaola quickly became an integral part of the school's football team, the Bulls, and was promoted to the varsity squad his sophomore year.  That same year, DePaola helped the Bulls win the 2A state championship in football.  DePaola's success continued into his senior year, in which he again led the football team to the state championship but ultimately lost.  As the team's quarterback, DePaola completed his senior year completing 68% of his passes, throwing 22 touchdowns, 2,092 passing yards, and allowing only 7 interceptions, leading his team to set a state record for single season scoring of 636 points.<ref name="Hunt Valley-Cockeysville Patch">{{cite web|url=http://patch.com/maryland/huntvalley/the-depaolas-hereford-high-family-legacy-comes-to-an-end|title=The DePaolas: Hereford High Family Legacy Comes to an End|date=April 28, 2011 |access-date=December 9, 2014}}</ref> In addition to receiving the Baltimore County Offensive Player of the Year award from The Baltimore Sun, DePaola also received honors as an all-Metro and All-State player.<ref name="Hereford Harbringer"/> The last football game DePaola would play during his high school career would be the Good Samaritan Bowl hosted at the [[Navy–Marine Corps Memorial Stadium]] in [[Annapolis, Maryland]].<ref name="The Baltimore Sun">{{cite web|url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2005/06/12/having-fun-for-last-time-east-wins-in-football-35-23/|title=Having 'fun' for last time, East wins in football, 35-23|work=The Baltimore sun|date=June 12, 2005 |access-date=December 9, 2014}}</ref>  While DePaola did make football his athletic focus during his high school career, he continued to play baseball earning all-Metro honors his senior year after batting .527 and posting a 3–1 record as a pitcher.<ref name="CBS Sports">{{cite web|url=http://www.cbssports.com/nfl/draft/players/historical/1693451|title=Andrew DePaola|publisher=CBS|access-date=December 9, 2014}}</ref>

After high school, DePaola went on to [[Rutgers University]] and joined the football team as a walk-on.<ref name="Scarlet Scuttlebutt">{{cite web|url=http://blogs.mycentraljersey.com/rutgers/2009/08/29/the-long-snapper-a-rutgers-tale/|title=The Long Snapper (a Rutgers tale)|access-date=December 9, 2014}}</ref> His first year, DePaola was [[redshirted]], a technique in player management for college sports in which students may practice with the team while attending classes, but not play in any games.<ref name="Hereford Harbringer"/> During his first two seasons on the team, including his redshirt season, DePaola served as the team's third string [[quarterback]], helping the team prepare for games during practices.  DePaola served as the team's holder on field goals during his third season, not once dropping the ball. It was during this season in 2007 when DePaola was featured on [[ESPN SportsCenter]] for a play in which DePaola received the ball for a field goal against the then #2 Ranked [[University of South Florida]], but instead completed a fifteen-yard pass for a touchdown.<ref name="Hereford Harbringer"/> DePaola began his fourth season with Rutgers as a wide receiver, but became the team's [[long snapper]] when the starting long snapper Jeremy Branch sustained a leg injury.<ref name="Scarlet Scuttlebutt"/> During the final four games of that season and for the entirety of his fifth season, DePaola served as the team's starting long snapper, playing in every game that final season.<ref name="Hereford Harbringer"/> DePaola went undrafted by a professional team after completing college.

===Tampa Bay Buccaneers===
DePaola was not immediately drafted after college, and would spend the next two years after graduation working as a [[bartender]] and other odd jobs before he'd get his break on an NFL roster.<ref>{{cite web|first=Courtney |last=Cronin |title=From family bar to Best Buy to the No. 2-ranked long-snapper: A Viking lives out his NFL dream |date=Nov 27, 2021 |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/minnesota-vikings/post/_/id/31494/from-family-bar-to-best-buy-to-the-no-2-ranked-long-snapper-a-viking-lives-out-his-nfl-dream |access-date=Nov 30, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Young |first=Lindsey |title=Behind the Pro Bowl Scenes with Andrew DePaola |date=Feb 8, 2023 |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/longform/andrew-depaola-pro-bowl-2023-behind-the-scenes |access-date=Nov 30, 2024}}</ref> DePaola first signed with the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] as a long snapper in early August 2012 during training camp, but after three weeks he was waived on August 27, 2012.<ref name="Bucs Ink 10 to Future Deals">{{cite web|url=http://www.buccaneers.com/news/article-1/Bucs-Ink-10-to-Future-Deals/a8738c67-c0a9-4e3f-9250-f389a7292dfc|title=Bucs Ink 10 to Future Deals|date=January 3, 2013|access-date=December 9, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150923195003/http://www.buccaneers.com/news/article-1/Bucs-Ink-10-to-Future-Deals/a8738c67-c0a9-4e3f-9250-f389a7292dfc|archive-date=September 23, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> On Thursday January 3, 2013, DePaola was signed to a future contract by the Buccaneers, meaning that at the start of the upcoming season DePaola would sign with the Buccaneers and be added to the active roster.<ref name="Bucs Ink 10 to Future Deals"/> DePaola was one of the final cuts in training camp in favor of long snapper [[Andrew Economos]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bucsnation.com/2013/8/31/4680226/andrew-depaola-cut-andrew-economos-wins-longsnapper-competition/in/4441377|title=Andrew DePaola cut; Andrew Economos wins longsnapper competition|date=August 31, 2013 |access-date=December 9, 2014 }}</ref> DePaola secured a starting role on May 14, 2014, signing full-time with the Buccaneers under a two-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.spotrac.com/nfl/tampa-bay-buccaneers/andrew-depaola/|title=Andrew DePaola|access-date=December 9, 2014 }}</ref> DePaola made his on-field debut against the [[Carolina Panthers]] on September 7, 2014, with two snaps on successful extra point attempts and one tackle assist.<ref>{{cite web|title=Game Center|url=http://www.buccaneers.com/schedule-and-events/game/2014/regular1|access-date=December 9, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141207191958/http://www.buccaneers.com/schedule-and-events/game/2014/regular1/|archive-date=December 7, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> He went on to be the long snapper for the Buccaneers for three seasons from 2014 to 2016.

On August 22, 2017, DePaola re-signed with the Buccaneers, only to be released on September 1, 2017, during final roster cuts.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bucs Bring Back DePaola, Waive Adjei-Barimah|url=http://www.buccaneers.com/news/article-smith/Bucs-Bring-Back-DePaola-Waive-Adjei-Barimah/6c7bc284-7acd-40bd-92ea-7880b4b21afa|author=Smith, Scott|website=Buccaneers.com|date=August 22, 2017|access-date=August 22, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170822170326/http://www.buccaneers.com/news/article-smith/Bucs-Bring-Back-DePaola-Waive-Adjei-Barimah/6c7bc284-7acd-40bd-92ea-7880b4b21afa|archive-date=August 22, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Bucs Start Roster Trim with D-Line Moves|url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/bucs-start-roster-trim-with-d-line-moves-19302378|author=Smith, Scott|website=Buccaneers.com|date=September 1, 2017|access-date=September 1, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170902005939/http://www.buccaneers.com/news/article-smith/Bucs-Start-Roster-Trim-with-D-Line-Moves/fc35d6cd-ac05-4f36-8650-7413e3c9e947|archive-date=September 2, 2017|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Chicago Bears===
On September 3, 2017, DePaola was claimed off waivers by the [[Chicago Bears]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Bears claim three players off waivers|url=http://www.chicagobears.com/news/article-1/Bears-claim-three-players-off-waivers/638b3665-97de-4e6c-94cd-980ad3dff5a0|author=Mayer, Larry|website=ChicagoBears.com|date=September 3, 2017|access-date=September 4, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170904201947/http://www.chicagobears.com/news/article-1/Bears-claim-three-players-off-waivers/638b3665-97de-4e6c-94cd-980ad3dff5a0|archive-date=September 4, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Oakland Raiders===
On March 16, 2018, DePaola signed a four-year contract with the [[Oakland Raiders]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Raiders sign LS Andrew DePaola to four-year deal|url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2018/03/16/raiders-sign-ls-andrew-depaola-to-four-year-deal/|author=Alper, Josh|website=ProFootballTalk.NBCSports.com|date=March 16, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.raiders.com/news/article-1/Raiders-Sign-Long-Snapper-Andrew-DePaola/ba3c0c2e-1ee6-414f-b378-505cd433ebdd|title=Raiders Sign Long Snapper Andrew DePaola|work=Raiders.com|date=March 16, 2018|access-date=March 18, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180318110349/http://www.raiders.com/news/article-1/Raiders-Sign-Long-Snapper-Andrew-DePaola/ba3c0c2e-1ee6-414f-b378-505cd433ebdd|archive-date=March 18, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> In Week 1, DePaola suffered a torn ACL and was placed on [[injured reserve]] on September 12, 2018.<ref>{{cite web|title=Raiders sign Bryant and Sieg; place DePaola on IR and waive Hatcher|url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-sign-bryant-and-sieg-place-depaola-on-ir-and-waive-hatcher|website=Raiders.com|date=September 12, 2018}}</ref>

On August 25, 2019, DePaola was released by the Raiders.<ref>{{cite web|title=Raiders sign Liuget and Allen-Williams; release DePaola and place Doug Martin on IR|url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-sign-liuget-and-allen-williams-release-depaola-and-place-doug-martin-on-|website=Raiders.com|date=August 25, 2019}}</ref>

===Carolina Panthers===
On August 28, 2019, DePaola was signed by the [[Carolina Panthers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Panthers place Destiny Vaeao on IR, sign Andrew DePaola|url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2019/08/28/panthers-place-destiny-vaeao-on-ir-sign-andrew-depaola/|author=Williams, Charean|work=Pro Football Talk|publisher=NBC Sports|date=August 28, 2019}}</ref> He was released during final roster cuts on August 30, 2019.<ref>{{cite news |author=Henson, Max |title=Panthers announce first wave of 2019 roster cuts |url=https://www.panthers.com/news/panthers-announce-first-wave-of-2019-roster-cuts-artis-payne-corn-elder |website=Panthers.com |date=August 30, 2019 |access-date=August 30, 2019}}</ref>

After sitting out the [[2019 NFL season]], DePaola had a tryout with the [[Houston Texans]] on August 20, 2020.<ref>{{cite tweet |user=AlbertBreer |title=Today’s tryout/visit list. |number=1296557572107968514 |date=August 20, 2020 |accessdate=August 21, 2020}}</ref>

===Minnesota Vikings===
On November 21, 2020, DePaola was signed to the [[practice squad]] of the [[Minnesota Vikings]].<ref name="Nov21">{{cite news |title=Vikings Activate FB C.J. Ham, Announce Roster Moves |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/vikings-activate-fb-c-j-ham-announce-roster-moves |website=Vikings.com |date=November 21, 2020 |access-date=December 27, 2020}}</ref> He was elevated to the active roster on November 21 and November 28 for the team's weeks 11 and 12 games against the [[Dallas Cowboys]] and Panthers, and reverted to the practice squad after each game.<ref name="Nov21"/><ref>{{cite tweet |user=Vikings |title=The #Vikings have elevated practice squad LS @andrewdepaola and TE @B_Dillon44 to the active roster for tomorrow's game. @swervinirvin_ has been downgraded to out. |number=1332791493203877893 |date=November 28, 2020 |accessdate=January 7, 2021}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on December 2, 2020.<ref>{{cite web|title=Vikings Activate Adam Thielen from Reserve/COVID-19 list; Announce Roster Moves|url=https://www.vikings.com/news/adam-thielen-reserve-covid19-sign-andrew-depaola|website=Vikings.com|date=December 2, 2020}}</ref> DePaola earned both a [[Pro Bowl]] selection and first-team [[All-Pro]] nomination as long snapper with the Vikings for the [[2022 NFL season|2022 season]].<ref name="All-Pro">{{Cite web|last=Young |first=Lindsey |title=Vikings Long Snapper Andrew DePaola Named to All-Pro 2nd Team |date=Jan 12, 2024 |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/long-snapper-andrew-depaola-all-pro-2nd-team |access-date=Nov 30, 2024}}</ref>

On March 14, 2023, DePaola signed a three-year contract extension with the Vikings.<ref>{{cite web|title=Andrew DePaola & Vikings Agree to Terms to Return All-Pro Long Snapper|url=https://www.vikings.com/news/vikings-agree-to-terms-with-ls-andrew-depaola|author=Young, Lindsey|website=Vikings.com|date=March 14, 2023}}</ref> He was awarded his second consecutive Pro Bowl selection and a second-team All-Pro nomination for the [[2023 NFL season|2023 season]].<ref name="All-Pro" />

On November 4, 2024, it was announced that DePaola would undergo surgery to repair a hand injury.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Vikings lose All-Pro long snapper DePaola for at least a month, might need a sub for kicker Reichard|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/minnesota/news/vikings-lose-all-pro-long-snapper-depaola/|access-date=November 8, 2024|website=cbsnews.com|language=en}}</ref> Despite a shortened season, DePaola was named first-team All-Pro and earned Pro Bowl honors once again, becoming the first long snapper to earn three consecutive Pro Bowl selections.<ref>{{cite web |last=Premo |first=Cole |website=CBSNews.com |title=Here are the Vikings named to 2025 Pro Bowl Games |date=Jan 2, 2025 |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/minnesota/pictures/gallery-vikings-named-to-2025-pro-bowl-games/ |access-date=Jan 10, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |website=APNews.com |title=2024 NFL All-Pro Team: See who made the roster |date=Jan 10, 2025 |url=https://apnews.com/article/nfl-all-pro-2024-cdf9837431c51929b072c357988bc024 |access-date=Jan 10, 2025}}</ref>

On March 10, 2026, DePaola re-signed with the Vikings on a one-year, $1.725 million contract.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Peters |first1=Craig |title=Vikings Agree to Terms with Long Snapper Andrew DePaola |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/andrew-depaola-long-snapper-2026-contract |website=vikings.com |access-date=11 March 2026}}</ref>

'''Andre Rishard Williams''' (born August 28, 1992) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[running back]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Boston College Eagles football|Boston College Eagles]]. He was a finalist for the 2013 [[Heisman Trophy]], and won the 2013 [[Doak Walker Award]] as the nation's best running back. During the 2013 season, Williams became only the 16th player in [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]] history to [[Rush (gridiron football)|rush]] for over 2,000 yards and he finished his college career ranked fifth all-time for most yards rushed in a single season with 2,177 yards. He was selected by the [[New York Giants]] in the fourth round of the [[2014 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Williams was born on August 28, 1992, in [[Poughkeepsie, New York]], to [[Jamaicans|Jamaican]] immigrants Lancelene and Ervin. Williams spent his first year in [[Jamaica]] before returning to live in [[Central Jersey]] with his parents, sister, and two brothers. His family also lived in [[Atlanta]] and [[Allentown, Pennsylvania]].<ref name="NYTimes">{{Cite web |last=Pennington |first=Bill |date=July 27, 2014 |title=Budding Author and Inventor Emerges Quickly in Giants' Backfield |url=https://www.nytimes.com/ |access-date=September 14, 2014 |website=The New York Times |archive-date=August 14, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220814223627/https://www.nytimes.com/ |url-status=live }}</ref> "By the eighth grade," Williams later explained, "I decided I was going to play [[Division I (NCAA)|Division I]] football."<ref name=NYTimes />

After transferring from [[Harrison High School (Kennesaw, Georgia)|Harrison High School]] in [[Kennesaw, Georgia]], Williams attended [[Parkland High School (Pennsylvania)|Parkland High School]] in [[South Whitehall Township, Pennsylvania]]. As a senior, he had 1,913 [[Rush (gridiron football)|rushing]] yards on 128 [[Carry (gridiron football)|carries]] and 33 [[touchdowns]] for the [[high school football|football]] team.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Harris |first=Jon |date=July 21, 2021 |title=Former NFL running back Andre Williams, a Parkland grad, leaves the game behind to open Promenade Shops business, putting 'morality over profit' |url=https://www.mcall.com/business/mc-biz-former-nfl-running-back-andre-williams-opening-denim-store-at-promenade-20210721-zdf6dxtrofgjrncx64banrhez4-story.html |access-date=February 27, 2023 |website=The Morning Call |language=en-US |archive-date=July 31, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220731210146/https://www.mcall.com/business/mc-biz-former-nfl-running-back-andre-williams-opening-denim-store-at-promenade-20210721-zdf6dxtrofgjrncx64banrhez4-story.html |url-status=live }}</ref>  He earned All-State Class AAAA first-team honors as a senior [[running back]] and was selected as ''[[The Morning Call]]'' Player of the Year. He led Parkland High School to a 10–3 record in 2009.

In addition to football, he was also a standout athlete for Parkland High School's [[track and field]] team. At the 2010 Pennsylvania 3A state championship, he finished third in the state in the [[100 meters]] with a time of 10.76 seconds<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL Football / Track |url=http://footballtalentadvisors.com/blog/category/nflfbtrack/ |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140809205110/http://footballtalentadvisors.com/blog/category/nflfbtrack/ |archive-date=August 9, 2014 |access-date=July 28, 2014 |website=Football Talent Advisors}}</ref> and second in the state in the [[200 meters]] with a time of 22.01 seconds.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Williams, Andre |url=http://parser.dyestat.com/search.jsp?athID=117480 |access-date=February 27, 2023 |website=DyeStat.com |archive-date=March 3, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303221608/http://parser.dyestat.com/search.jsp?athID=117480 |url-status=live }}</ref> He was also timed at 14.61 seconds in the [[110 meter hurdles]] in 2009.

In 2010, Williams was ranked a three-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]] and was rated the 44th best running back prospect in the nation.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andre Williams, 2010 Running Back |url=https://rivals.com/content/athletes/andre-williams-31012?view=pv |access-date=February 27, 2023 |website=Rivals.com |language=en-US |archive-date=February 27, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230227041300/https://n.rivals.com/content/athletes/andre-williams-31012?view=pv |url-status=live }}</ref> He committed to [[Boston College]] over offers from [[Temple University|Temple]], [[University of Akron|Akron]], and [[Vanderbilt University|Vanderbilt]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andre Williams, Boston College Eagles, Running Back |url=https://247sports.com/Player/Andre-Williams-3761/college-40505 |access-date=April 7, 2018 |website=247Sports |archive-date=February 27, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230227041247/https://247sports.com/Player/Andre-Williams-3761/college-40505/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

==College career==
[[File:Andre Williams (American football) 2012.jpg|thumb|Williams playing for [[Boston College Eagles football|Boston College]] in October 2012]]
Williams attended [[Boston College]], where he played for its [[Boston College Eagles|Eagles football]] team from 2010 to 2013.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andre Williams College Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/andre-williams-2.html |access-date=April 7, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=April 8, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180408141326/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/andre-williams-2.html |url-status=live }}</ref> He graduated early with a degree in [[applied psychology]] and [[human development theory|human development]].<ref name=NYTimes />

===Freshman season===
Williams's first three years at Boston College were relatively uneventful. Playing as a [[true freshman]] in 2010, Williams showed his potential while sharing the backfield with Montel Harris and Sterlin Phifer.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2010 Boston College Eagles Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/boston-college/2010.html |access-date=April 7, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=April 8, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180408073904/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/boston-college/2010.html |url-status=live }}</ref> He played in all 13 games, rushing for 461 yards on 95 carries with two touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andre Williams 2010 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/andre-williams-2/gamelog/2010/ |access-date=April 7, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=April 8, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180408141321/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/andre-williams-2/gamelog/2010/ |url-status=live }}</ref> In the final regular season game of the year, playing at [[Syracuse University|Syracuse]], he set the school record for rushing attempts in a game, running 42 times as the Eagles beat the Orange 16–7.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Boston College at Syracuse Box Score, November 27, 2010 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2010-11-27-syracuse.html |access-date=April 7, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=April 8, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180408073840/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2010-11-27-syracuse.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Sophomore season===
As a sophomore in 2011, Williams continued to improve, but played less time with sharing the backfield with Rolandon Finch, Tahj Kimble, and Montel Harris, starting seven of 10 games and rushing for 517 yards on 124 carries with four touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2011 Boston College Eagles Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/boston-college/2011.html |access-date=April 7, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=April 8, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180408075448/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/boston-college/2011.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Andre Williams 2011 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/andre-williams-2/gamelog/2011/ |access-date=April 7, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=April 8, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180408073859/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/andre-williams-2/gamelog/2011/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Junior season===
As a junior in 2012, he continued to be a reliable option, although for a pass-heavy offense, starting eight of nine games, rushing for 584 yards on 130 carries and four touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andre Williams 2012 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/andre-williams-2/gamelog/2012/ |access-date=April 7, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=April 8, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180408073647/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/andre-williams-2/gamelog/2012/ |url-status=live }}</ref> His efforts were mostly in vain though, as the Eagles continued to progressively get worse, winning 7 games in 2010, 4 in 2011, and only 2 in 2012.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2012 Boston College Eagles Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/boston-college/2012.html |access-date=April 7, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=April 8, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180408073613/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/boston-college/2012.html |url-status=live }}</ref> His three years of experience, however would pave the way for his breakout senior year and a turnaround for the Eagles team.

===Senior season===
With a change in coaching during the offseason, [[Steve Addazio]] brought in new coordinators and a new style of offense focused heavily on the run.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Boston College Eagles Football Record By Year |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/boston-college/ |access-date=April 7, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=April 8, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180408073609/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/boston-college/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Williams started off the year as a powerful weapon, running for 114 and 204 yards respectively in wins over [[Villanova Wildcats football|Villanova]] and [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons football|Wake Forest]], and scoring once in each game.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Villanova at Boston College Box Score, August 31, 2013 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2013-08-31-boston-college.html |access-date=April 7, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=April 8, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180408073626/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2013-08-31-boston-college.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Wake Forest at Boston College Box Score, September 6, 2013 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2013-09-06-boston-college.html |access-date=April 7, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=April 8, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180408073558/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2013-09-06-boston-college.html |url-status=live }}</ref> He had his worst performance of the season against a strong [[USC Trojans football|USC]] defense, managing only 38 yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Boston College at USC Box Score, September 14, 2013 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2013-09-14-southern-california.html |access-date=April 7, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=April 8, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180408075445/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2013-09-14-southern-california.html |url-status=live }}</ref> However, he bounced back against #8 ranked [[Florida State Seminoles football|Florida State]] and ran for 149 yards as the Eagles nearly upset the eventual National Champions.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Florida State at Boston College Box Score, September 28, 2013 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2013-09-28-boston-college.html |access-date=April 7, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=April 8, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180408075452/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2013-09-28-boston-college.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

The following week, during the Homecoming game against [[Army Black Knights football|Army]], Williams exploded offensively, scoring five touchdowns and rushing for 263 yards, only 1 yard shy of the school's single game rushing record. He momentarily tied the record, but unfortunately lost a yard on his last rushing attempt of the game, bringing his total back down.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Army at Boston College Box Score, October 5, 2013 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2013-10-05-boston-college.html |access-date=April 7, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=April 8, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180408073809/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2013-10-05-boston-college.html |url-status=live }}</ref> After rushing for only 70 yards at [[Clemson Tigers football|Clemson]], he gave two solid performances against [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill|UNC]] and [[Virginia Tech Hokies football|Virginia Tech]], rushing for 172 and 166 yards, respectively, and scoring three times.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Boston College at Clemson Box Score, October 12, 2013 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2013-10-12-clemson.html |access-date=April 7, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=April 8, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180408073940/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2013-10-12-clemson.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Boston College at North Carolina Box Score, October 26, 2013 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2013-10-26-north-carolina.html |access-date=April 7, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=April 8, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180408073814/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2013-10-26-north-carolina.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Virginia Tech at Boston College Box Score, November 2, 2013 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2013-11-02-boston-college.html |access-date=April 7, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=April 8, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180408141256/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2013-11-02-boston-college.html |url-status=live }}</ref> The next week at [[New Mexico State Aggies football|New Mexico State]], Williams managed to break the single game record that he came so close to during the Army game, running for 295 yards and two scores.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Vega |first=Michael |date=November 10, 2013 |title=Andre Williams rushes for school-record 295 yards to carry BC past New Mexico State |url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/sports/colleges/2013/11/10/andre-williams-rushes-for-school-record-yards-carry-past-new-mexico-state/4eDjqrSidlf7nF7Z09VZiK/story.html |access-date=February 26, 2023 |website=[[The Boston Globe]] |archive-date=August 3, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210803184451/https://www.bostonglobe.com/sports/colleges/2013/11/10/andre-williams-rushes-for-school-record-yards-carry-past-new-mexico-state/4eDjqrSidlf7nF7Z09VZiK/story.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Boston College at New Mexico State Box Score, November 9, 2013 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2013-11-09-new-mexico-state.html |access-date=April 7, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=April 8, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180408073836/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2013-11-09-new-mexico-state.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

The following week, playing on senior day, Boston College's final home game of the season against [[NC State Wolfpack football|NC State]], Williams broke his own record and ran for 339 yards on 42 carries, scoring twice.<ref>{{Cite web |title=North Carolina State at Boston College Box Score, November 16, 2013 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2013-11-16-boston-college.html |access-date=April 7, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=April 8, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180408073844/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2013-11-16-boston-college.html |url-status=live }}</ref> The performance also surpassed the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC) record, previously set at 329 yards by John Leach of Wake Forest in 1993. During the game, he also broke the school's single season record for rushing yards, finishing the day with 1,810 yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2013 FBS (I-A) College Football Individual Statistics Leaders for Rushing - ESPN |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/stats/player/_/stat/rushing/season/2013/group/80 |access-date=February 26, 2023 |website=ESPN.com |archive-date=February 27, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230227041211/https://www.espn.com/college-football/stats/player/_/stat/rushing/season/2013/group/80 |url-status=live }}</ref> The win made BC bowl eligible for the first time since 2010, and tripled the previous year's win total, prompting the students and fans to rush the field and celebrate with the team following the win. Williams's performance was recognized by media across the country, as he was named the Walter Camp National Player of the Week, as well as ACC offensive back of the week.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 17, 2013 |title=Boston College's Andre Williams and North Carolina's Kareem Martin Named Walter Camp National Players of the Week, presented by Generation UCAN |url=https://waltercamp.org/boston-colleges-andre-williams-and-north-carolinas-kareem-martin-named-walter-camp-national-players-of-the-week-presented-by-generation-ucan/ |access-date=February 27, 2023 |website=Walter Camp Football Foundation |language=en-US |archive-date=December 23, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211223183706/https://waltercamp.org/boston-colleges-andre-williams-and-north-carolinas-kareem-martin-named-walter-camp-national-players-of-the-week-presented-by-generation-ucan/ |url-status=live }}</ref> His successes and statistics as the league's leading rusher made him the front-runner for the [[Doak Walker Award]] as the nation's best running back.

After the success against North Carolina State at home, the Eagles took on [[Maryland Terrapins football|Maryland]] for the first of their final two road games of the season. Williams had another big day, running for 263 yards and two scores, passing 2,000 yards and becoming only the 16th player in NCAA history to accomplish this feat.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Boston College at Maryland Box Score, November 23, 2013 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2013-11-23-maryland.html |access-date=April 7, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=April 8, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180408073920/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2013-11-23-maryland.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Patterson |first=Chip |date=November 23, 2013 |title=Andre Williams breaks 2,000-yard mark in Boston College win |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-football/news/andre-williams-breaks-2000-yard-mark-in-boston-college-win/ |access-date=February 27, 2023 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en |archive-date=February 27, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230227041212/https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/college-basketball-rankings-grades-another-a-for-kentucky-michigan-earns-a-b-and-virginia-gets-f/xhr/?showTaboola=false |url-status=live }}</ref> With this achievement, Williams became a part of the [[Heisman Trophy]] conversation.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cooper |first=Sam |date=November 23, 2013 |title=Boston College's Andre Williams passes 2,000-yard mark, enters Heisman race |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/ncaaf-dr-saturday/boston-college-andre-williams-passes-2-000-yard-020946221--ncaaf.html |access-date=February 26, 2023 |website=Yahoo! Sports |archive-date=July 29, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210729085517/https://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/ncaaf-dr-saturday/boston-college-andre-williams-passes-2-000-yard-020946221--ncaaf.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Vint |first=Patrick |date=November 23, 2013 |title=Andre Williams for Heisman |url=https://www.sbnation.com/college-football/2013/11/23/5138408/andre-williams-boston-college-heisman-trophy |access-date=February 27, 2023 |website=SBNation.com |language=en |archive-date=May 18, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220518093120/https://www.sbnation.com/college-football/2013/11/23/5138408/andre-williams-boston-college-heisman-trophy |url-status=live }}</ref>

The final game of the regular season was at 5–6 [[Syracuse Orange football|Syracuse]]. Unfortunately, Williams re-aggravated a right shoulder injury that he had been dealing with since the UNC game. He left the game early in the 3rd quarter and did not return, having rushed for only 29 yards for the day. Despite the disappointing end to the game, those 29 yards put Williams over 2,100 yards for the season and placed him at 9th all time in the FBS single-season rushing list.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Boston College at Syracuse Box Score, November 30, 2013 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2013-11-30-syracuse.html |access-date=April 7, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=April 8, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180408073535/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2013-11-30-syracuse.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

The Eagles final game of the season was in the [[2013 Independence Bowl]] against the [[2013 Arizona Wildcats football team|Arizona Wildcats]]. The game featured a matchup between the nation's two best running backs in Williams and Arizona's [[Ka'Deem Carey]], who was a consensus [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] in 2012 as well as a finalist for the 2013 Doak Walker award, which Williams won. The game was a blowout win for Arizona, as they cruised to a 42–19 victory. Williams ran for 75 yards in his final contest as a college back, finishing with 2,177 yards on the season, 5th most all-time in the NCAA.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Independence Bowl - Arizona vs Boston College Box Score, December 31, 2013 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2013-12-31-boston-college.html |access-date=April 7, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=April 8, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180408073856/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2013-12-31-boston-college.html |url-status=live }}</ref>
