===New York Giants===
The [[New York Giants]] selected Williams in the fourth round with the 113th overall pick of the [[2014 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2014 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2014/draft.htm |access-date=April 7, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=September 21, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180921123401/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2014/draft.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> He made his NFL debut in the season opener against the [[Detroit Lions]]. In the 35–14 loss, he had five carries for nine yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=New York Giants at Detroit Lions - September 8th, 2014 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201409080det.htm |access-date=April 7, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=June 13, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180613160522/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201409080det.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

On September 25, in a 45–14 victory over the [[Washington Redskins]], he scored his first professional rushing touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=New York Giants at Washington Redskins - September 25th, 2014 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201409250was.htm |access-date=April 7, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=April 8, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180408073744/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201409250was.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> On December 7, against the Tennessee Titans, he had 24 carries for 131 rushing yards and a rushing touchdown in the 36–7 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=New York Giants at Tennessee Titans - December 7th, 2014 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201412070oti.htm |access-date=April 7, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=April 8, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180408073703/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201412070oti.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> Overall, he finished his rookie season with 721 rushing yards and seven rushing touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andre Williams 2014 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/W/WillAn00/gamelog/2014/ |access-date=April 7, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=April 8, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180408073556/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/W/WillAn00/gamelog/2014/ |url-status=live }}</ref> His production dipped in his second season as he recorded 88 carries for 257 yards and a rushing touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andre Williams 2015 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/W/WillAn00/gamelog/2015/ |access-date=April 7, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=April 8, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180408073359/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/W/WillAn00/gamelog/2015/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He was released by the team on September 3, 2016.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 3, 2016 |title=Notable cuts roundup: Giants cut Andre Williams |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/notable-cuts-roundup-texans-cut-wideout-cecil-shorts-0ap3000000694974 |access-date=September 3, 2016 |website=[[NFL.com]] |archive-date=September 4, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160904012454/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000694974/article/notable-cuts-roundup-giants-cut-andre-williams |url-status=live }}</ref>

===San Diego/Los Angeles Chargers===
On September 4, 2016, the [[San Diego Chargers]] claimed Williams off waivers.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Henne |first=Ricky |date=September 4, 2016 |title=Chargers Add Three via Waivers |url=http://www.chargers.com/news/2016/09/04/chargers-add-three-waivers?sf35113673=1 |access-date=February 26, 2023 |website=Chargers.com |archive-date=April 8, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180408073615/http://www.chargers.com/news/2016/09/04/chargers-add-three-waivers?sf35113673=1 |url-status=live }}</ref> He was released on September 24, 2016,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Henne |first=Ricky |date=September 24, 2016 |title=Chargers Promote TE Asante Cleveland to Active Roster; Waive RB Andre Williams |url=http://www.chargers.com/news/2016/09/24/chargers-promote-te-asante-cleveland-active-roster-waive-rb-andre-williams |access-date=February 26, 2023 |website=Chargers.com |archive-date=April 8, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180408073832/http://www.chargers.com/news/2016/09/24/chargers-promote-te-asante-cleveland-active-roster-waive-rb-andre-williams |url-status=live }}</ref> and was signed to the [[practice squad]] two days later. He was promoted to the active roster on December 27, 2016.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Henne |first=Ricky |date=December 27, 2016 |title=Bolts Make Trio of Running Back Transactions |url=https://www.chargers.com/news/bolts-make-trio-of-running-back-transactions-144701 |access-date=February 26, 2023 |website=Chargers.com |archive-date=July 26, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210726053217/https://www.chargers.com/news/bolts-make-trio-of-running-back-transactions-144701 |url-status=live }}</ref> He appeared in the regular season finale against the Kansas City Chiefs and had 18 carries for 87 rushing yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kansas City Chiefs at San Diego Chargers - January 1st, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201701010sdg.htm |access-date=April 7, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=January 31, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180131080953/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201701010sdg.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

On March 9, 2017, the Chargers re-signed Williams.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bouda |first=Nate |date=March 9, 2017 |title=Chargers Re-Signing RB Andre Williams - NFLTradeRumors.co |url=http://nfltraderumors.co/chargers-re-signing-rb-andre-williams/ |access-date=March 10, 2017 |website=NFLTradeRumors.co |language=en-US |archive-date=March 10, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170310103656/http://nfltraderumors.co/chargers-re-signing-rb-andre-williams/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He was waived on September 2, 2017, and was signed to the Chargers' practice squad the next day.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Henne |first=Ricky |date=September 2, 2017 |title=Los Angeles Chargers Cut Down Roster to 53 |url=http://www.chargers.com/news/2017/09/02/los-angeles-chargers-cut-down-roster-53 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171228125650/http://www.chargers.com/news/2017/09/02/los-angeles-chargers-cut-down-roster-53 |archive-date=December 28, 2017 |access-date=February 26, 2023 |website=Chargers.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Henne |first=Ricky |date=September 3, 2017 |title=Chargers Announce First Members of 2017 Practice Squad |url=http://www.chargers.com/news/2017/09/03/chargers-announce-first-members-2017-practice-squad |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180412221838/http://www.chargers.com/news/2017/09/03/chargers-announce-first-members-2017-practice-squad |archive-date=April 12, 2018 |access-date=February 26, 2023 |website=Chargers.com}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on October 7, 2017.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Henne |first=Ricky |date=October 7, 2017 |title=Bolts Sign RB Andre Williams; Waive S Dexter McCoil |url=http://www.chargers.com/news/2017/10/07/bolts-sign-rb-andre-williams-waive-s-dexter-mccoil |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180603111845/http://www.chargers.com/news/2017/10/07/bolts-sign-rb-andre-williams-waive-s-dexter-mccoil |archive-date=June 3, 2018 |access-date=February 26, 2023 |website=Chargers.com}}</ref> In Week 14, Williams suffered a broken wrist on the final play of the game and was ruled out for the rest of the 2017 season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Williams |first=Charean |author-link=Charean Williams |date=December 11, 2017 |title=Andre Williams out for year with broken wrist |url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2017/12/11/andre-williams-out-for-year-with-broken-wrist/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210801145234/https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2017/12/11/andre-williams-out-for-year-with-broken-wrist/ |archive-date=August 1, 2021 |access-date=February 26, 2023 |website=ProFootballTalk}}</ref> He was placed on [[injured reserve]] on December 12, 2017.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Henne |first=Ricky |date=December 12, 2017 |title=Chargers Announce Trio of Transactions |url=http://www.chargers.com/news/2017/12/12/chargers-announce-trio-transactions |access-date=February 26, 2023 |website=Chargers.com |archive-date=May 20, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180520013441/http://www.chargers.com/news/2017/12/12/chargers-announce-trio-transactions |url-status=live }}</ref> Overall, he finished the 2017 season with nine carries for 25 yards in eight games.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andre Williams 2017 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/W/WillAn00/gamelog/2017/ |access-date=April 7, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=April 8, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180408073849/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/W/WillAn00/gamelog/2017/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Houston Roughnecks===
Williams was selected by the [[Houston Roughnecks (2020)|Houston Roughnecks]] of the [[XFL (2020)|XFL]] in the 9th round in the [[2020 XFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bender |first=Bill |date=October 21, 2019 |title=XFL Draft picks 2019: Complete results, rosters, players for new football league |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/nfl/news/xfl-draft-tracker-results-picks-list-rosters-football-league/jahz8p84e4i61hb8lajqs4a22 |access-date=October 22, 2019 |website=[[Sporting News]] |archive-date=December 4, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201204214328/https://www.sportingnews.com/us/nfl/news/xfl-draft-tracker-results-picks-list-rosters-football-league/jahz8p84e4i61hb8lajqs4a22 |url-status=live }}</ref> He had his contract terminated when the league suspended operations on April 10, 2020.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Condotta, Bob |date=April 10, 2020 |title=XFL suspends operations, terminates all employees, but Jim Zorn says he has hopes league will continue |work=SeattleTimes.com |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/xfl-suspends-operations-terminates-all-employees/ |access-date=July 17, 2020 |archive-date=March 7, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210307104736/https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/xfl-suspends-operations-terminates-all-employees/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Personal life==
Since his college years, Williams had been writing what he calls  a "philosophical memoir", which is titled ''A King, a Queen and a Conscience''. As of 2014, he expected to complete the manuscript in 2015, but it has not been published. Williams also sought to secure a patent for a "compression shirt" type of athletic gear that could improve backfield running.<ref name=NYTimes />

In 2014, Williams married Carolyn Jay, who also attended [[Boston College]]. His first child, Barron Zavier, was born in February 2016. Six months later, Williams and Jay filed for divorce. In 2018, Williams had a second son, Ka'el Malik, with his longtime friend Deshonia Peavy.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hortillosa |first=Summer Dawn |date=September 2, 2014 |title=Giants running back Andre Williams ties the knot at Secaucus Town Hall |url=http://www.nj.com/hudson/index.ssf/2014/09/giants_running_back_andre_williams_ties_the_knot_at_secaucus_town_hall.html |access-date=November 2, 2017 |website=NJ.com |language=en-US |archive-date=November 7, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171107033249/http://www.nj.com/hudson/index.ssf/2014/09/giants_running_back_andre_williams_ties_the_knot_at_secaucus_town_hall.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=June 12, 2016 |title=Andre Williams, No. 44 of NY Giants, Tackles Fatherhood and Serves Food for Thought |url=http://www.theroot.com/andre-williams-no-44-of-ny-giants-tackles-fatherhood-1790855618 |access-date=November 2, 2017 |website=The Root |language=en-US |archive-date=November 7, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171107025720/http://www.theroot.com/andre-williams-no-44-of-ny-giants-tackles-fatherhood-1790855618 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Smith High School]] in [[Chesapeake, Virginia]]. He has been a member of the [[Cincinnati Bengals]], [[Houston Texans]], [[Indianapolis Colts]], [[Tennessee Titans]], [[Los Angeles Chargers]], [[Arizona Cardinals]], [[Chicago Bears]] and [[Buffalo Bills]]. == Early life == A native of [[Chesapeake, Virginia]], Brown initially attended [[Indian River High School (Chesapeake, Virginia)|Indian River High School]] for his freshman and sophomore year. He transferred to Oscar Smith his junior year. At Oscar Smith, Brown further developed into one of the most sought-after prospects in the country. After posting 83 [[tackled gridiron|tackles]] and 11 [[qb sack|sack]]s in 2012, he was named a first-team [[All-American]] by ''[[USA Today]]'', a rare feat for a junior. In his senior year, Brown recorded 93 tackles, 30 for a loss, 18 sacks and forced nine [[fumble]]s. Oscar Smith went undefeated into the 2013 VHSL 6A state championship game, where they were upset by [[Centreville High School (Fairfax County, Virginia)|Centreville High School]] 35–6.{{Cite news |last=Parker |first=Brandon |date=December 14, 2013 |title=Centreville topples Oscar Smith for Virginia 6A football championship |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/highschools/centreville-topples-oscar-smith-for-virginia-6a-football-championship/2013/12/14/3e66fa32-64fd-11e3-a373-0f9f2d1c2b61_story.html |access-date=2025-08-11 |work=[[The Washington Post]]}} Brown repeated as ''USA Today'' All-American and also was named the [[Gatorade High School Football Player of the Year]] in 2013.[http://www.usatodayhss.com/article/andrew-brown-2013-gatorade-national-football-player-of-the-year Andrew Brown named Gatorade National Football Player of the Year] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131213052501/http://www.usatodayhss.com/article/andrew-brown-2013-gatorade-national-football-player-of-the-year |date=December 13, 2013 }}{{Cite web |url=http://www.dailypress.com/sports/teel-blog/dp-teel-time-andrew-brown-gatorade,0,1490586.post |title=Teel Time: U.Va. recruit Andrew Brown named national football player of year |access-date=December 13, 2013 |archive-date=February 21, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140221172820/http://www.dailypress.com/sports/teel-blog/dp-teel-time-andrew-brown-gatorade,0,1490586.post |url-status=dead }} Regarded as a five-star recruit, Brown was ranked as the number one [[defensive tackle]] in his class.[https://sports.yahoo.com/ncaa/football/recruiting/player-Andrew-Brown-116735 Rivals.com] He committed to the [[University of Virginia]].[https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/football/story/_/id/9436684/dt-andrew-brown-no-3-overall-recruit-commits-virginia-cavaliers Andrew Brown commits to Virginia] ==College career== Brown played for the Cavaliers from 2014 through 2017. '''Andrew Alexander McDonald''' (born September 8, 1988) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was an [[offensive tackle]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Indiana Hoosiers football|Indiana Hoosiers]] and was undrafted before beginning his NFL career with the [[Miami Dolphins]] in 2012.<ref name="IU Profile">{{cite web|url=http://www.iuhoosiers.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/mcdonald_andrew00.html |title=Andrew McDonald Bio |publisher=Indiana University |accessdate=February 18, 2014 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140222004251/http://www.iuhoosiers.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/mcdonald_andrew00.html |archivedate=February 22, 2014 }}</ref><ref name="Dolphins signing">{{cite web | url=http://articles.sun-sentinel.com/2012-05-14/sports/sfl-miami-dolphins-announce-signing-of-ot-andrew-mcdonald-20120514_1_jeff-ireland-dolphins-tryout-miami-dolphins | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140222061710/http://articles.sun-sentinel.com/2012-05-14/sports/sfl-miami-dolphins-announce-signing-of-ot-andrew-mcdonald-20120514_1_jeff-ireland-dolphins-tryout-miami-dolphins | url-status=dead | archive-date=February 22, 2014 | title=Miami Dolphins announce signing of OT Andrew McDonald | publisher=Sun Sentinel | date=May 14, 2012 | accessdate=February 18, 2014 | author=Gould, Izzy}}</ref>

===Miami Dolphins===
After going undrafted, McDonald was invited to participate in the [[Miami Dolphins]]' rookie mini-camp. In May 2012, he was officially signed by the team.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thephinsider.com/2012/5/14/3020469/miami-dolphins-sign-tackle-andrew-mcdonald|title=Miami Dolphins Sign Tackle Andrew McDonald|date=May 14, 2012|first=Kevin|last=Nogle|accessdate=2014-09-09}}</ref>

===Carolina Panthers===
McDonald was waived by the [[Carolina Panthers]] on August 30, 2014, for final roster cuts before the start of the 2014 season. He was signed to the team's practice squad the next day.<ref>{{cite web|work=Panthers.com|url=http://www.panthers.com/news/article-2/Panthers-sign-10-to-practice-squad/ff910cc5-507a-4654-8b0d-31f05cd88db9|title=Panthers sign 10 to practice squad|date=August 31, 2014|first=Bryan|last=Strickland|accessdate=2014-09-02}}</ref>

===Seattle Seahawks===
On September 9, 2014, McDonald was signed away from the Panthers practice squad by the [[Seattle Seahawks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fieldgulls.com/2014/9/8/6121483/seahawks-sign-ot-andrew-mcdonald-per-his-agent|title=Seahawks sign OT Andrew McDonald|date=Sep 9, 2014|first=Danny|last=Kelly|accessdate=2014-09-09}}</ref>

===Indianapolis Colts===
McDonald signed with the [[Indianapolis Colts]] on December 2, 2014.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Wilkening|first1=Mike|title=Colts sign OT Andrew McDonald, waive TE Weslye Saunders|url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2014/12/02/colts-sign-ot-andrew-mcdonald-waive-te-weslye-saunders/|publisher=Pro Football Talk|accessdate=2 December 2014}}</ref>

===Cleveland Browns===
McDonald was claimed off of waivers by the [[Cleveland Browns]] on December 16, 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nationalfootballpost.com/Browns-add-Andrew-McDonald-cut-Zac-Diles.html|title=Browns Add Andrew McDonald, cut Zac Diles|last=Wilson|first=Aaron|publisher=National Football Post|date=December 16, 2014|accessdate=December 16, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141217010208/http://www.nationalfootballpost.com/Browns-add-Andrew-McDonald-cut-Zac-Diles.html|archive-date=December 17, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> On September 5, 2015, he was waived by the Browns.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/article-5/Cleveland-Browns-reduce-roster-to-53/b0ce17ea-8cc1-4597-a8f6-4dd192677a6b |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171107084154/http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/article-5/Cleveland-Browns-reduce-roster-to-53/b0ce17ea-8cc1-4597-a8f6-4dd192677a6b |url-status=dead |archive-date=November 7, 2017 |title=Cleveland Browns reduce roster to 53 |date=September 5, 2015 |website=ClevelandBrowns.com |accessdate=September 25, 2015}}</ref> On the following day, he cleared waivers and was signed to the Browns' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/article-5/Browns-sign-eight-to-practice-squad/8ac64188-2db2-45a7-8302-63b7a80e97b0 |title=Browns sign eight to practice squad |author=<!--Staff writer(s); ===Houston Texans===
McDonald was signed by the [[Houston Texans]] January 4, 2016 to play in their Wild Card match up, against the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] in place of the injured [[Duane Brown]]. On September 3, 2016, he was released by the Texans.<ref>{{cite web|title=TRANSACTIONS: Texans down to 53-man roster|url=http://www.houstontexans.com/news/article-2/TRANSACTIONS-Texans-down-to-53-man-roster/134830f6-5c30-4d46-9d18-8cbd723fb17f|website=HoustonTexans.com|access-date=2016-09-03|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170826234400/http://www.houstontexans.com/news/article-2/TRANSACTIONS-Texans-down-to-53-man-roster/134830f6-5c30-4d46-9d18-8cbd723fb17f|archive-date=2017-08-26|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===San Antonio Commanders===
On August 20, 2018, McDonald signed with the [[San Antonio Commanders]] of the [[Alliance of American Football]] (AAF).<ref>{{cite web|last=Songer|first=Cameron|url=https://www.kens5.com/article/sports/former-reagan-qb-highlights-list-of-11-players-added-to-san-antonio-pro-football-roster/273-586066598|title=Former Reagan QB highlights list of 11 players added to San Antonio pro football roster|publisher=[[KENS]]|date=August 21, 2018|accessdate=February 4, 2019}}</ref> The league ceased operations in April 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rothstein |first=Michael |last2=Wickersham |first2=Seth |date=June 13, 2019 |title=Inside the short, unhappy life of the Alliance of American Football |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/26957796/inside-short-unhappy-life-alliance-american-football |access-date=January 9, 2024 |website=[[ESPN.com]]}}</ref>

===St. Louis BattleHawks===
In October 2019, McDonald was selected by the [[St. Louis BattleHawks]] in the open phase of the [[2020 XFL draft]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Talbot|first=Damond|url=https://www.nfldraftdiamonds.com/2019/10/xfl-draft-8/|title=XFL Draft Phase 5: The Final Rounds of the Draft, Find out who was selected|publisher=NFL Draft Diamonds|date=October 16, 2019|accessdate=October 23, 2019}}</ref> He had his contract terminated when the league suspended operations on April 10, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |author=Condotta, Bob |title=XFL suspends operations, terminates all employees, but Jim Zorn says he has hopes league will continue |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/xfl-suspends-operations-terminates-all-employees/ |website=SeattleTimes.com |date=April 10, 2020 |accessdate=July 17, 2020}}</ref>

==Personal life==
McDonald was identified in the Wells Report as "Player A," one of the personnel hazed by [[Richie Incognito#Bullying scandal|Richie Incognito]] and other members of the Dolphins.<ref name="Wells Report">{{cite web | url=https://www.si.com/si-wire/2014/02/15/andrew-mcdonald-player-a-incognito-report | title=Andrew McDonald says he is 'Player A' in Incognito report, has "no problem" with Dolphin organization | publisher=Sports Illustrated | date=February 15, 2014 | accessdate=February 18, 2014 | author=Maldy, Brendan}}</ref>

In May 2014, McDonald underwent surgery to treat cancer. He recovered in time to participate in the Panthers 2014 training camp.<ref name="Cancer Surgery">{{cite web | url=http://www.cbssports.com/nfl/eye-on-football/24591830/panthers-ot-andrew-mcdonald-undergoes-cancer-surgery | title=Panthers OT Andrew McDonald undergoes cancer surgery | work=CBS Sports | date=June 18, 2014 | accessdate=July 3, 2014 | author=Katzowitz, Josh}}</ref>

'''Andrew Jackson''' (born March 16, 1992) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was selected by the [[Indianapolis Colts]] in the sixth round of the [[2014 NFL draft]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Western Kentucky Hilltoppers football|Western Kentucky Hilltoppers]].

==College career==
Jackson played [[college football]] for the [[Western Kentucky Hilltoppers football|Western Kentucky Hilltoppers]].

==Professional career==

===Indianapolis Colts===
Jackson was selected by the Colts in the sixth round (203rd overall) of the [[2014 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2014 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2014/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-15 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He played in 13 games during the 2014 season, making 10 total tackles and one quarterback sack.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andrew Jackson 2014 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/J/JackAn02/gamelog/2014/ |access-date=2025-10-03 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He was waived on February 11, 2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://fox59.com/2015/02/11/colts-release-safety-laron-landry-two-other-players/|title=Colts release safety LaRon Landry, waive two other players|last=Adams|first=Matt|work=fox59.com|date=February 11, 2015|accessdate=February 11, 2015}}</ref>

===Spokane Empire===
On August 30, 2016, Jackson signed with the [[Spokane Empire]] of the [[Indoor Football League]].

===Memphis Express===
In 2019, Jackson joined the [[Memphis Express]] of the [[Alliance of American Football]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Munz|first=Jason|url=https://www.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/2019/02/08/aaf-memphis-express-birmingham-iron-5-things-know-trent-richardson-alliance-football-hackenberg/2765881002/|title=AAF: Memphis Express at Birmingham Iron – 5 things to know|newspaper=[[The Commercial Appeal]]|date=February 8, 2019|accessdate=February 19, 2019}}</ref> In the fourth game of the [[2019 AAF season]] against the [[San Diego Fleet]], Jackson recorded 14 tackles, a sack, and an interception as the Express won 26–23; he was later named AAF Defensive Player of the Week.<ref>{{cite web|last=Stuchbery|first=Fran|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/farrow-memphis-pair-earn-aaf-honors-for-week-four/n-5454653|title=Farrow, Memphis Pair Earn AAF Honors for Week Four|publisher=Out Sports Central|date=March 5, 2019|accessdate=March 5, 2019}}</ref> The league ceased operations in April 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rothstein |first=Michael |last2=Wickersham |first2=Seth |date=June 13, 2019 |title=Inside the short, unhappy life of the Alliance of American Football |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/26957796/inside-short-unhappy-life-alliance-american-football |access-date=January 9, 2024 |website=[[ESPN.com]]}}</ref>

===Houston Roughnecks===
Jackson was selected in the 7th round during phase three in the 2020 XFL draft by the [[Houston Roughnecks (2020)|Houston Roughnecks]].<ref>{{cite web|title=DEFENSIVE FRONT SEVEN DRAFT TRACKER|url=https://www.xfl.com/en-US/articles/phase-3-defensive-front-seven-draft-tracker|website=XFL.com|date=October 14, 2019}}</ref> He was waived during final roster cuts on January 22, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |author=Talbot, Damond |title=A Full List of XFL Roster Cuts, Who was released today? |url=https://www.nfldraftdiamonds.com/2020/01/xfl-transactions-9/ |website=NFLDraftDiamonds.com |date=January 22, 2020 |accessdate=January 23, 2020}}</ref>

===St. Louis BattleHawks===
Jackson signed with the [[St. Louis BattleHawks]] on February 18, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |title=XFL Transactions |url=https://www.xfl.com/xfl-transactions |website=XFL.com |accessdate=February 18, 2020}}</ref> His contract was terminated when the league suspended operations on April 10, 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Condotta |first=Bob |date=April 10, 2020 |title=XFL suspends operations, terminates all employees, but Jim Zorn says he has hopes league will continue |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/xfl-suspends-operations-terminates-all-employees/ |access-date=July 17, 2020 |website=SeattleTimes.com}}</ref>

===Duke City Gladiators===
Jackson signed with the [[Duke City Gladiators]] on April 27, 2021.

===Baltimore Ravens===
On November 13, 2017, Donnal was claimed off waivers by the [[Baltimore Ravens]], reuniting him with Iowa teammate [[Carl Davis (American football)|Carl Davis]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Ravens Claim Offensive Tackle Andrew Donnal|url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/ravens-claim-offensive-tackle-andrew-donnal-19764318|author=Downing, Garrett|website=BaltimoreRavens.com|date=November 13, 2017}}</ref> He was waived on August 31, 2018.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ravens Release 10 Players, Send Four to Injured Reserve|url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/ravens-release-10-players-send-four-to-injured-reserve|author=Mink, Ryan|website=BaltimoreRavens.com|date=August 31, 2018}}</ref>

On September 2, 2018, Donnal was claimed off waivers by the [[Detroit Lions]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Lions awarded OL Andrew Donnal and CB Dee Virgin via waivers|url=https://www.detroitlions.com/news/lions-awarded-ol-andrew-donnal-and-cb-dee-virgin-via-waivers|website=DetroitLions.com|date=September 2, 2018|access-date=September 3, 2018|archive-date=September 4, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180904052518/https://www.detroitlions.com/news/lions-awarded-ol-andrew-donnal-and-cb-dee-virgin-via-waivers|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On September 24, 2019, Donnal was signed by the [[Miami Dolphins]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Dolphins Sign Andrew Donnal, Release Tank Carradine|url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/dolphins-sign-andrew-donnal-release-tank-carradine|website=MiamiDolphins.com|date=September 24, 2019}}</ref> He was waived on November 16, 2019.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dolphins Activate Julién Davenport Off Injured Reserve|url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/dolphins-activate-julien-davenport-off-injured-reserve|website=MiamiDolphins.com|date=November 16, 2019|access-date=November 17, 2019|archive-date=November 17, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191117024541/https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/dolphins-activate-julien-davenport-off-injured-reserve|url-status=dead}}</ref>

'''Andrew Dean East''' (born September 17, 1991) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[long snapper]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL).  He played [[college football]] for the [[Vanderbilt Commodores football|Vanderbilt Commodores]], and had multiple stints with various NFL teams, including the [[Washington Redskins]].

== Early life ==
East was named a captain of the [[North Central High School (Indianapolis)|North Central High School]] football team in Indianapolis, Indiana. He was a three-year starter on defense and special teams for the 5A division school in the Indianapolis area.

When East was a sophomore and junior, he started at the linebacker position, posting 110 tackles as a junior. He was named the All-Around-Area linebacker while starting as a long-snapper.

As a senior, East contributed 64 tackles and seven quarterback sacks as a first-year starter. He also received the Indiana Academic All-State honors award.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://vucommodores.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/05/vand_m_footbl_2013_14_misc_non_event__2013_FB_Factbook_Players.pdf|title=The Players of 2013|last=|first=|year=2013|website=Vanderbilt Athletics|publisher=Vanderbilt University|location=Nashville, Tennessee|orig-year=|via=Vanderbilt Football Through the Years|access-date=December 1, 2019}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Kansas City Chiefs===
East signed with the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] on May 11, 2015.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/college/2015/05/03/tsu-vanderbilt-wku-players-sign-free-agents/26819033|title=TSU, Vanderbilt, WKU players sign as free agents|work=Tennessean.com|date=May 2, 2015|access-date=May 3, 2015}}</ref> He was released by the Chiefs on August 30, 2015.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Thorman|first1=Joel|url=https://www.arrowheadpride.com/2015/8/30/9228281/chiefs-roster-cuts-first-11-players-have-been-released|title=Chiefs roster cuts: First 11 players have been released|publisher=SBNation|website=ArrowheadPride.com|date=August 30, 2015|access-date=August 31, 2015}}</ref>

===Seattle Seahawks===
East signed a reserve/future contract with the [[Seattle Seahawks]] on January 4, 2016.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Larrabee|first1=Kirk|url=https://247sports.com/Bolt/Reports-Seattle-Seahawks-sign-three-to-reserve-future-deals-42552132|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160109105409/http://247sports.com/Bolt/Reports-Seattle-Seahawks-sign-three-to-reserve-future-deals-42552132|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 9, 2016|title=Reports: Seattle Seahawks sign three to reserve-future deals|website=247Sports.com|date=January 4, 2016|access-date=April 26, 2016}}</ref> He was waived on March 24, 2016.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Condotta|first1=Bob|url=http://www.seattletimes.com/sports/seahawks/seahawks-waive-andrew-east-as-team-continues-to-make-long-snapping-moves|title=Seahawks waive Andrew East as team continues to make long-snapping moves|work=SeattleTimes.com|date=March 24, 2016|access-date=April 26, 2016}}</ref>

===Oakland Raiders===
East was signed by the [[Oakland Raiders]] on April 5, 2016.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Damien|first1=Levi|url=https://www.silverandblackpride.com/2016/4/5/11371230/oakland-raiders-add-long-snapper-andrew-east|title=Raiders add long snapper Andrew East|publisher=SBNation|website=SilverAndBlackPride.com|date=April 5, 2016|access-date=April 26, 2016}}</ref> He was waived by the team on August 29, 2016.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Damien|first1=Levi|url=https://www.silverandblackpride.com/2016/8/29/12699638/oakland-raiders-cuts-2016-roster-trimmed-to-75|title=Raiders cuts 2016: Roster trimmed to 75|publisher=SBNation|website=SilverAndBlackPride.com|date=August 29, 2016|access-date=August 29, 2016}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Rams===
On March 13, 2017, East signed with the [[Los Angeles Rams]].<ref>{{cite web|title=LA Rams Solidify Super Bowl Trajectory By Signing Backup Long Snapper Andrew East|url=https://www.turfshowtimes.com/2017/3/14/14927902/la-rams-long-snapper-andrew-east-super-bowl-dynasty-greatest-snap-on-turf|author=McAtee, Joe|website=TurfShowTimes.com|date=March 14, 2017}}</ref> On May 3, 2017, he was waived by the Rams.<ref>{{cite web|title=LA Rams Cut Four Players on Wednesday, Sign Former 49er|url=https://www.turfshowtimes.com/2017/5/3/15537960/la-rams-2017-roster-cuts-four-players-sign-49ers-nt-mike-purcell|author=Bate, Brandon|website=TurfShowTimes.com|date=May 3, 2017}}</ref>

===Oakland Raiders (second stint)===
On July 28, 2017, East was signed by the Raiders.<ref>{{cite web|title=Raiders Sign Andrew East; Release Austin Howard, Taiwan Jones|url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-sign-andrew-east-release-austin-howard-taiwan-jones-19065890|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171231203723/http://www.raiders.com/news/article-1/Raiders-Sign-Andrew-East-Release-Austin-Howard-Taiwan-Jones/46c86d8f-4cbe-4539-a1df-100c2d40371d|url-status=live|archive-date=December 31, 2017|website=Raiders.com|date=July 28, 2017|access-date=February 25, 2022}}</ref> He was waived on September 2, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Raiders Announce Transactions|url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-announce-transactions-19070584|website=Raiders.com|date=September 2, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171209084351/http://www.raiders.com/news/article-1/Raiders-Announce-Transactions/f671cc9c-caa3-429f-992e-5629667b4dec|archive-date=December 9, 2017|access-date=February 25, 2022}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract with the Raiders on January 19, 2018.<ref>{{cite web|title=Raiders sign LS Andrew East to reserve/future contract|url=https://raiderswire.usatoday.com/2018/01/19/raiders-sign-ls-andrew-east-to-reserve-future-contract/|website=USAToday.com|date=January 19, 2018}}</ref> He was waived by the Raiders on April 9, 2018.<ref>{{cite web|title=Raiders waive Andrew East|url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2018/04/09/raiders-waive-andrew-east/|author=Williams, Charean|website=ProFootballTalk|date=April 9, 2018}}</ref>

===Jacksonville Jaguars===
On June 14, 2018, East signed with the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Jaguars make roster moves|url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/jaguars-make-roster-moves|website=Jacksonville Jaguars|date=June 14, 2018}}</ref> He was waived on July 31, 2018.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jaguars Sign Tight End Deandre Goolsby|url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/jaguars-sign-tight-end-deandre-goolsby|website=Jacksonville Jaguars|date=July 31, 2018}}</ref>

=== Memphis Express ===
On November 9, 2018, East was allocated to the [[Memphis Express]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/2018/11/09/aaf-andrew-east-olympic-gold-medalist-shawn-johnson-husband-added-express-roster/1942742002/|title=AAF: Andrew East, Olympic gold medalist Shawn Johnson's husband, boards Memphis Express|work=The Commercial Appeal|access-date=November 9, 2018|language=en}}</ref>

===Washington Redskins===
On December 15, 2018, East was signed by the [[Washington Redskins]] after long snapper [[Nick Sundberg]] was placed on injured reserve due to a back injury.<ref>{{cite web|title=Redskins Sign Matt Flanagan, Joshua Holsey, Andrew East; Waive Kapri Bibbs, Marcus Smith|url=https://www.commanders.com/news/redskins-sign-matt-flanagan-josh-holsey-andrew-east-waive-kapri-bibbs-marcus-smi|website=Washington Commanders|date=December 15, 2018|access-date=February 25, 2022|archive-date=February 3, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220203065512/https://www.commanders.com/news/redskins-sign-matt-flanagan-josh-holsey-andrew-east-waive-kapri-bibbs-marcus-smi|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was waived on August 2, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.commanders.com/news/redskins-sign-dj-white-waive-andrew-east |title=Redskins Sign DB D.J. White, Waive LS Andrew East |date=August 2, 2019 |website=Washington Commanders|access-date=February 25, 2022}}</ref>

He announced his retirement in a video on his family’s [[YouTube]] channel on February 25, 2022.<ref>{{cite web |author=The East Family |title=retiring from the NFL |url=https://m.youtube.com/watch?v=BCYM6NMxK6g |website=YouTube |access-date=February 26, 2022 |date=February 25, 2022}}</ref>

==Personal life==
East is married to Olympic gymnast and gold medalist [[Shawn Johnson East|Shawn Johnson]]. East and Johnson were engaged on July 24, 2015, at [[Wrigley Field]] during a [[Chicago Cubs]] game,<ref>{{cite web|last1=Rayne|first1=Naja|url=https://people.com/celebrity/shawn-johnson-engaged-to-andrew-east/|title=Shawn Johnson Engaged to Andrew East|website=People|date=July 24, 2015|access-date=February 25, 2022}}</ref> and were married on April 16, 2016, in [[Franklin, Tennessee]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Finan|first=Eileen|url=https://people.com/sports/shawn-johnson-marries-andrew-east/|title=Shawn Johnson Marries NFL Player Andrew East|website=People|date=April 16, 2016|access-date=February 25, 2022}}</ref> The couple live in [[Nashville, Tennessee]]. '''Andrew Franks''' (born January 11, 1993) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[placekicker]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was signed by the [[Miami Dolphins]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2015. He played [[college football]] for the [[RPI Engineers football|RPI Engineers]].

==College career==
Franks attended [[Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute]] (RPI), a [[Division III (NCAA)|Division III]] school, from 2011 to 2014.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.rpiathletics.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=6931|title=Andrew Franks – 2014 Football|access-date=May 2, 2016}}</ref> He was twice named first-team [[All-American]] by D3football.com, one of two All-America teams recognized in the [[NCAA]] record book.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.d3football.com/awards/all-americans/all-time|title=D3football.com: All-time All-Americans|access-date=September 6, 2017}}</ref> He received a bachelor's degree in biomedical engineering.{{Cn|date=December 2025}}

== Professional career ==
===Miami Dolphins===
In May 2015, the [[Miami Dolphins]] signed Franks as an undrafted free agent to compete along with [[Caleb Sturgis]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.montereyherald.com/sports/20150502/dolphins-sign-carmel-kicker-andrew-franks|title=Dolphins sign Carmel kicker Andrew Franks|website=www.montereyherald.com|access-date=May 2, 2016}}</ref>  On September 5, 2015, Franks won the job, after Sturgis was released.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://fantasynews.cbssports.com/fantasyfootball/update/25291686/dolphins-keep-andrew-franks-cut-caleb-sturgis|title=Dolphins keep Andrew Franks, cut Caleb Sturgis - CBSSports.com|website=CBSSports.com|access-date=May 2, 2016}}</ref> At the end of the 2015 season, Franks had converted 81.2% of his [[field goals]] (13-of-16) and kicked 33 [[extra points]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nfl.com/player/andrewfranks/2553648/careerstats|title=Andrew Franks: Career Stats at NFL.com|website=www.nfl.com|access-date=May 2, 2016}}</ref>

Franks remained the Dolphins' kicker during the 2016 season. During Week 14, he made his first game-winning field goal, kicking a 21-yard field goal to win the game 26–23 over the [[Arizona Cardinals]] with 1 second remaining on the clock. In Week 16, he hit his career high field goal from 55 yards against the [[Buffalo Bills]] on December 24, 2016 to tie the game at 31–31 with 10 seconds remaining.<ref name="q918">{{cite web | agency=Associated Press | title=Franks' FG seals Miami's victory | website=Arkansas Online | date=2016-12-25 | url=https://www.arkansasonline.com/news/2016/dec/25/franks-fg-seals-miami-s-victory-2016122/ | access-date=2024-12-27}}</ref> Franks later kicked a 27-yard field goal late in overtime to win the game.<ref name="j579">{{cite web | last=Diaz | first=Al | title=Epic! Miami Dolphins beat Buffalo Bills 34-31 in overtime | website=Miami Herald | date=2016-12-24 | url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/nfl/miami-dolphins/article122866259.html | access-date=2025-01-18}}</ref> On September 3, 2017, he was waived by the Dolphins.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dolphins Make Roster Moves|url=http://m.miamidolphins.com/s/30855/269?itemUri=837436073/1341298731115012181101213253|website=MiamiDolphins.com|date=September 3, 2017|access-date=September 27, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170904111856/http://m.miamidolphins.com/s/30855/269?itemUri=837436073%2F1341298731115012181101213253|archive-date=September 4, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Tampa Bay Vipers===
In October 2019, Franks was selected by the [[Tampa Bay Vipers]] of the [[XFL (2020)|XFL]] in the open phase of the [[2020 XFL draft]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Talbot|first=Damond|url=https://www.nfldraftdiamonds.com/2019/10/xfl-draft-8/|title=XFL Draft Phase 5: The Final Rounds of the Draft, Find out who was selected|publisher=NFL Draft Diamonds|date=October 16, 2019|accessdate=October 23, 2019}}</ref> He had his contract terminated when the league suspended operations on April 10, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |author=Condotta, Bob |title=XFL suspends operations, terminates all employees, but Jim Zorn says he has hopes league will continue |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/xfl-suspends-operations-terminates-all-employees/ |website=SeattleTimes.com |date=April 10, 2020 |accessdate=July 17, 2020}}</ref>

'''Andrew Mitchell Billings''' (born March 6, 1995) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[nose tackle]] for the [[Arizona Cardinals]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Baylor Bears football|Baylor Bears]] and was selected by the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] in the fourth round of the [[2016 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Billings attended [[Waco High School]] in [[Waco, Texas]]. He was rated by [[Rivals.com]] as a four-star recruit and committed to [[Baylor University]] to play [[college football]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andrew Billings, 2013 Defensive Tackle, Baylor |url=https://rivals.com/content/athletes/andrew-billings-13047?view=pv |access-date=2024-07-06 |website=Rivals.com |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>[http://collegesportsblog.dallasnews.com/2013/02/andrew-billings-chooses-to-play-college-football-for-the-baylor-bears.html/ Andrew Billings chooses Baylor Bears over Texas Longhorns, TCU Horned Frogs] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130507084204/http://collegesportsblog.dallasnews.com/2013/02/andrew-billings-chooses-to-play-college-football-for-the-baylor-bears.html/ |date=May 7, 2013 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Werner |first=John |last2=Ash |first2=David |date=2013-02-05 |title=Baylor hooks big recruit in Billings |url=https://wacotrib.com/baylor-hooks-big-recruit-in-billings/article_3ee04848-daaa-5c72-8cd9-351b5907c7b9.html |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Waco Tribune-Herald |language=en}}</ref> Billings also competed in [[powerlifting]] during high school and broke [[Mark Henry]]'s Texas record with 2,010 pounds. The record was set with an 805-pound squat, 500-pound bench press, and a 705-pound dead lift.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/blog/big12/post/_/id/92538 Athletic freak Andrew Billings playing big role for Baylor]</ref><ref>[http://www.wvgazettemail.com/article/20151014/GZ02/151019701/1115 Billings gives Baylor defense a big lift]</ref>

==College career==
As a [[true freshman]] at Baylor in 2013, Billings played in 11 games and made two starts while recording 29 total [[Tackle (football move)#Gridiron football|tackles]].<ref>[http://www.wacotrib.com/sports/baylor/football/big-ol-billings-rushing-the-qb-or-clogging-running-lanes/article_dd9887b9-bb2f-543f-835c-8833224b5e13.html Big ol' Billings: Rushing the QB or clogging running lanes, Bears DT disrupts offenses]</ref> As a sophomore in 2014, he started all 13 games and was named 1st Team [[List of All-Big 12 Conference football teams|All-Big 12 Conference]] after recording 37 tackles and two [[Quarterback sack|sacks]].<ref>[https://www.espn.com/blog/big12/post/_/id/101491 Shawn Oakman, Andrew Billings form ideal alliance for Baylor]</ref> In his 2015 junior season, he started in 12 games, posting career highs in total tackles (39), solo tackles (31), [[tackles for loss]] (14), and sacks (5.5). His efforts earned him Big 12 Co-Defensive Player of the Year (shared with [[Emmanuel Ogbah]]), Big 12 Defensive Lineman of the Year, and 1st Team All-Big 12 Conference honors.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2015-12-09 |title=2015 All-Big 12 Football Awards Announced |url=https://big12sports.com/news/2015/12/9/210570297.aspx |access-date=2024-10-07 |website=big12sports.com |language=en}}</ref> Billings finished his college career with 106 total tackles, 14 tackles for loss, 8 sacks, and 2 forced fumbles.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andrew Billings College Stats, School, Draft, Gamelog, Splits |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/andrew-billings-1.html |access-date=2024-10-07 |website=College Football at Sports-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Pre-draft===
As a top [[defensive tackle]] prospect, Billings chose to forego his senior season and would receive an invitation to the [[NFL Scouting Combine|NFL Combine]]. He attended the combine and completed all of the required combine drills. [[Fox Sports]] listed him as one of their top five biggest winners from the combine and his performance was perceived well overall by scouts for his display of raw strength coupled with exceptional quickness and speed for a man of his size.<ref>{{cite web| title=5 biggest winners from the NFL Scouting Combine| url=https://www.foxsports.com/nfl/story/nfl-combine-winners-carson-wentz-william-jackson-will-fuller-andrew-billings-jalen-ramsey-022916| access-date=November 19, 2017| website=foxsports.com| date=February 29, 2016}}</ref> On March 16, 2016, Billings participated at Baylor's [[Pro Day]] along with [[Corey Coleman]], [[Shawn Oakman]], [[Spencer Drango]], [[Xavien Howard]], Grant Campbell, [[LaQuan McGowan]], [[Jimmy Landes]], and seven other teammates.<ref>{{cite web| title=FOOTBALL HOLDS 2016 PRO DAY| url=http://www.baylorbears.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/031616aad.html| access-date=November 19, 2017| website=baylorbears.com| last=Hill| first=Jerry| archive-date=December 1, 2017| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201032054/http://www.baylorbears.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/031616aad.html| url-status=dead}}</ref> A record 61 team representatives and scouts from all 32 NFL teams attended Baylor's pro day, including general manager [[Kevin Colbert]] ([[Pittsburgh Steelers]]) and head coaches [[Mike Tomlin]] (Steelers) and [[Bill O'Brien (American football)|Bill O'Brien]] ([[Houston Texans]]). Billings performed well and chose to run the [[40-yard dash]] (4.96), 20-yard dash (2.89), 10-yard dash (1.76), [[short shuttle]] (4.78), and [[three-cone drill]] (7.74) and decreased his times from the combine in all of them. At the conclusion of the pre-draft process, Billings was projected to be a late-first- or second-round pick. He was ranked the third-best defensive tackle prospect in the draft by [[ESPN]], the sixth-best defensive tackle by NFLDraftScout.com and NFL analyst [[Mike Mayock]], and was ranked the seventh-best defensive lineman by ''[[Sports Illustrated]]''.<ref>{{cite web| title=*Andrew Billings, DS #6 DT, Baylor| url=http://www.nfldraftscout.com/ratings/dsprofile.php?pyid=126668&draftyear=2016&genpos=dt| access-date=November 19, 2017| website=nfldraftscout.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=2016 NFL draft position rankings| url=https://www.si.com/nfl/2016/04/12/nfl-draft-2016-position-rankings-players-prospects| access-date=November 19, 2017| newspaper=Sports Illustrated}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| title=Mayock's top 100 draft prospect rankings| url=https://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000655903/article/mike-mayocks-2016-nfl-draft-top-100-prospect-rankings| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160427132844/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000655903/article/mike-mayocks-2016-nfl-draft-top-100-prospect-rankings| url-status=dead| archive-date=April 27, 2016| access-date=November 19, 2017| website=NFL.com| last=Mayock |first=Mike| date=April 27, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| title=Ranking the Draft's Top 100 Players| url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/draft2016/story/_/id/15290519| access-date=November 19, 2017| website=ESPN.com| last=Legwold |first=Jeff| date=April 25, 2016}}</ref> He drew major interest and was linked to the [[Green Bay Packers]], [[Washington Redskins]], Steelers, and [[Minnesota Vikings]].<ref name="stunning"/><ref>{{cite web| title=After meeting Steelers, Andrew Billings talks football with Steelers Wire| url=https://www.steelerswire.usatoday.com/2016/03/21/after-meeting-with-steelers-baylor-dt-andrew-billings-talks-with-steelers-wire/amp/| access-date=November 19, 2017| website=steelerwire.usatoday.com| last=Chester |first=Simon A.}}{{Dead link|date=September 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

===Cincinnati Bengals===
====2016====
The [[Cincinnati Bengals]] selected Billings in the fourth round (122nd overall) of the [[2016 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Bengals 2016 Draft Results: Cincinnati Bengals select defensive tackle Andrew Billings in Round 4|url=https://www.cincyjungle.com/nfldraft/2016/4/30/11540210/bengals-2016-draft-results-cincinnati-bengals-select-defensive-tackle-andrew-billings|last=Cosenza |first=Anthony|website=CincyJungle.com|date=April 30, 2016|access-date=November 21, 2017}}</ref> He was the 16th defensive tackle selected in 2016.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2016 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2016/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-17 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> His fall in the draft was greatly unexpected as no teams gave any indications of it prior to the draft. He was projected as a first rounder in multiple mock drafts by [[Pro Football Focus]] and NFL analysts [[Todd McShay]] and [[Mel Kiper Jr.]]<ref>{{cite web| title=What Caused Hyped NFL Draft Prospects Andrew Billings, Connor Cook to Fall?| url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2636848-what-caused-hyped-nfl-draft-prospects-andrew-billings-connor-cook-to-fall| access-date=November 19, 2017| website=bleacherreport.com| last=McCrystal |first=Ryan| date=April 30, 2016}}</ref> There were many speculations that ranged from his lack of height and size for his position and a possible knee injury. Bengals head coach [[Marvin Lewis]] said "I think his height maybe was restrictive in some ways for some people at times but we've done pretty well these guys." Billings stated in regards to his fall in the draft, "This is something I'm going to carry with me my whole life." "It's actually a good thing for me." He drew comparisons, by multiple media outlets, to teammate [[Geno Atkins]] and his equally unexpected slide in the draft during the [[2010 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Bengals get Andrew Billings, a DT with penchant for pancakes, in fourth round|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/cincinnati-bengals/post/_/id/22523| access-date=November 19, 2017| website=ESPN.com|date=April 30, 2016}}</ref><ref name="stunning">{{cite web| title=Andrew Billings' stunning draft fall has the Bengals DT thinking payback| url=https://www.espn.com/blog/cincinnati-bengals/post/_/id/22526| access-date=November 19, 2017| website=ESPN.com| last=Harvey |first=Coley| date=May 2, 2016}}</ref>

On May 18, 2016, the Bengals signed Billings to a four-year, $2.87 million contract that included a signing bonus of $535,845.<ref>{{cite web| title=Spotrac.com: Andrew Billings contract| url=http://www.spotrac.com/nfl/cincinnati-bengals/andrew-billings-19076/| access-date=November 19, 2017| website=spotrac.com}}</ref>

He competed with [[Domata Peko]], [[Pat Sims]], and [[DeShawn Williams]] throughout [[Training camp (NFL)|training camp]] for the starting nose tackle position. On August 10, 2016, he was carted off the field during the Bengals' practice after suffering a knee injury. On August 15, he underwent surgery to repair a torn [[meniscus (anatomy)|meniscus]] and was placed on [[injured reserve]] for the entirety of the season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Andrew Billings out indefinitely with torn meniscus|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/billings-expected-to-miss-season-with-torn-meniscus-0ap3000000685456|website=NFL.com|last=Sessler |first=Marc|date=April 30, 2016}}</ref> The Cincinnati Bengals later lost another rookie ([[William Jackson III]]) for the entire {{NFL Year|2016}}.

====2017====
Billings competed with Pat Sims, DeShawn Williams, and Josh Tupou throughout training camp for the vacant starting nose tackle position left by the departure of Domata Peko to the [[Denver Broncos]] during free agency.<ref>{{cite web| title=Ourlads.com: Cincinnati Bengals' depth chart: 09/01/2017| url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/197/CIN| access-date=November 19, 2017| website=Ourlads.com}}</ref> Head coach Marvin Lewis named him the backup nose tackle to Pat Sims to begin the regular season.<ref>{{cite web| title=Bengals release Week 1 depth chart: Joe Mixon RB3; Pat Sims starting at NT| url=https://www.cincyjungle.com/2017/9/5/16256140/bengals-week-1-depth-chart-joe-mixon-rb3-pat-sims-starting-nt| access-date=November 19, 2017| website=cincyjungle.com| last=Marcum |first=Jason| date=September 5, 2017}}</ref>

He made his professional regular season debut in the Bengals' season-opener against the [[Baltimore Ravens]] and recorded one solo tackle in their 20–0 loss. On November 24, 2017, Billings earned his first career start against the [[Tennessee Titans]] in place of Sims who had injured his calf the previous week.<ref>{{cite web| title=Bengals lose Pat Sims to calf injury vs Jaguars| url=https://www.cincyjungle.com/2017/11/5/16609662/bengals-pat-sims-calf-injury-jaguars-nfl-injury-report| access-date=November 19, 2017| website=cincyjungle.com| last=Marcum |first=Jason| date=November 5, 2017}}</ref> Billings recorded a season-high four combined tackles in the Bengals' 24–20 loss.<ref name="stats">{{cite web| title=NFL Player stats: Andrew Billings| url=http://www.nfl.com/player/andrewbillings/2555267/gamelogs| access-date=November 19, 2017| website=NFL.com}}</ref> Throughout the first seven games he played in 59 total defensive snaps and earned 48 defensive snaps against the Titans.<ref>{{cite web| title=Andrew Billings seizes the spotlight with Pat Sims hurt| url=https://www.bengalswire.usatoday.com/2017/11/11/andrew-billings-seizes-the-spotlight-with-pat-sims-hurt/amp/| access-date=November 19, 2017| website=cincyjungle.com| last=Zargar |first=Cameron}}{{Dead link|date=September 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

===Cleveland Browns===
[[File:Andrew Billings (2021).jpg|thumb|Billings with the Cleveland Browns in 2021]]
On March 26, 2020, Billings signed with the [[Cleveland Browns]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Browns add defensive tackle Andrew Billings|url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2020/03/19/browns-add-defensive-tackle-andrew-billings/|last=Gantt |first=Darin|work=Pro Football Talk|publisher=NBC Sports|date=March 19, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Browns add size to D-Line with signing of DT Andrew Billings|url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-add-size-to-d-line-with-signing-of-dt-andrew-billings|last=Gribble |first=Andrew|website=ClevelandBrowns.com|date=March 26, 2020}}</ref> He chose to opt-out of the 2020 season due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]] on August 4, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |title=Browns place DT Andrew Billings on Reserve/Opt-Out list |url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-place-dt-andrew-billings-on-reserve-opt-out-list |website=ClevelandBrowns.com |date=August 4, 2020 |access-date=August 4, 2020}}</ref>

Billings was waived by the Browns on November 13, 2021.<ref>{{cite news |title=Browns make roster moves |url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-make-roster-moves-x1207 |publisher=ClevelandBrowns.com |date=November 13, 2021 |access-date=November 13, 2021 |archive-date=November 13, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211113202221/https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-make-roster-moves-x1207 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Miami Dolphins===
On November 16, 2021, Billings was signed to the [[practice squad]] of the [[Miami Dolphins]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Roster Moves: Miami Dolphins Make Roster Moves|url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/roster-moves-miami-dolphins-make-roster-moves-x5166|website=MiamiDolphins.com|date=November 16, 2021}}</ref>

===Kansas City Chiefs===
On January 19, 2022, Billings was signed to the [[Kansas City Chiefs]]' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Chiefs make several practice squad transactions on Wednesday|url=https://chiefswire.usatoday.com/2022/01/19/kansas-city-chiefs-andrew-billings-roderick-johnson-signed-elijah-mcguire-released/|work=Chiefs Wire|publisher=USA Today|date=January 19, 2022}}</ref>

===Las Vegas Raiders===
On February 27, 2022, Billings signed with the [[Las Vegas Raiders]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Andrew Billings agrees to terms with Raiders|url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2022/02/27/andrew-billings-agrees-to-terms-with-raiders/|last=Williams |first=Charean|work=Pro Football Talk|publisher=NBC Sports|date=February 27, 2022}}</ref> He started all 14 games he played in and notched a career best 39 total tackles.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Andrew Billings (DT): Bio, News, Stats & more |url=https://www.chicagobears.com/team/players-roster/andrew-billings/ |access-date=2024-10-07 |website=ChicagoBears.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

===Chicago Bears===
On March 16, 2023, Billings signed with the [[Chicago Bears]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Roster Moves: Bears agree to terms with Billings, release Siemian|url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/roster-moves-bears-agree-to-terms-with-billings-release-siemian|last=Mayer |first=Larry|website=ChicagoBears.com|date=March 16, 2023}}</ref> On November 2, Billings signed a two-year contract extension worth $8.5 million, with $6 million guaranteed.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bears sign DT Andrew Billings to two-year extension|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/38802032/bears-sign-dt-andrew-billings-two-year-extension|last=Cronin|first=Courtney|website=ESPN.com|date=November 2, 2023}}</ref> He started all 17 games for the Bears during the [[2023 NFL season|2023 Season]] at defensive tackle.<ref name=":0" /> 

On September 15, 2024, Billings collected his first career forced fumble, using his helmet to knock the football out of the hands of [[Houston Texans]] [[running back]] [[Cam Akers]].<ref name="v588">{{cite web | last=Mayer | first=Larry | title=Andrew Billings making impact anchoring defensive line | website=Chicago Bears | date=2024-09-19 | url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/andrew-billings-making-impact-anchoring-defensive-line | access-date=2025-01-31}}</ref> On November 7, Billings was placed on injured reserve after undergoing surgery to repair a torn pectoral muscle.<ref name="o723">{{cite web | last=Cronin | first=Courtney | title=Bears NT Billings put on IR, likely out for season | website=ESPN.com | date=2024-11-07 | url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/42254495/bears-nt-andrew-billings-pec-put-ir-likely-season | access-date=2025-01-31}}</ref>

===Arizona Cardinals===
On March 16, 2026, Billings signed a one-year, $2.4 million contract with the [[Arizona Cardinals]].<ref>{{Cite web | date=March 16, 2026| last=Urban| first=Darren | title=Cardinals Load Up On Depth With Jack Gibbens, Andrew Billings| url=https://www.azcardinals.com/news/cardinals-load-up-on-depth-andrew-wingard-jack-gibbens-andrew-billings|website=azcardinals.com |access-date=March 16, 2026}}</ref>

'''Andrew Bonnet''' (born December 27, 1992) is an American former [[American football|football]] [[fullback (gridiron football)|fullback]]. He played [[college football]] at [[North Dakota State University]].

==Professional career==

===Carolina Panthers===
After going undrafted in the [[2016 NFL draft]], Bonnet signed with the [[Carolina Panthers]] on May 2, 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.panthers.com/news/article-2/panthers-agree-to-terms-with-seven-college-free-agents/2544ff28-b9a0-41bf-911a-65565700c3ca|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171222053149/http://www.panthers.com/news/article-2/panthers-agree-to-terms-with-seven-college-free-agents/2544ff28-b9a0-41bf-911a-65565700c3ca|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 22, 2017|title=Panthers agree to terms with seven college free agents|last=Strickland|first=Bryan|work=Panthers.com|date=May 2, 2016|accessdate=September 24, 2016}}</ref> On May 20, 2016, he was waived by the Panthers.

===Cincinnati Bengals===
Bonnet was then signed by the [[Cincinnati Bengals]]. On September 3, 2016, he was waived by the Bengals.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dehner Jr. |first=Paul |last2=Owczarski |first2=Jim |date=September 3, 2016 |title=Bengals cut down to 53-man roster, Hardison to IR |url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/nfl/bengals/2016/09/03/cincinnati-bengals-announce-final-cut-53/89824586/ |access-date=2023-11-14 |website=The Enquirer |language=en-US}}</ref>

===Philadelphia Eagles===
On September 5, 2016, Bonnet was signed to the [[practice squad]] of the [[Philadelphia Eagles]]. He was released on October 11, 2016. He later signed a reserve/future contract with the Eagles on January 12, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Eagles Add FB Andrew Bonnet|url=http://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/article-1/Eagles-Add-FB-Andrew-Bonnet-/c181cae1-1bea-4c89-8f54-7947a139f573|author=Smith, Alex|website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com|date=January 12, 2017|access-date=January 12, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170115191905/http://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/article-1/Eagles-Add-FB-Andrew-Bonnet-/c181cae1-1bea-4c89-8f54-7947a139f573|archive-date=January 15, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> On May 4, 2017, he was released by the Eagles.<ref>{{cite web |author=Mangels |first=Dave |date=May 4, 2017 |title=Eagles release three players |url=http://www.bleedinggreennation.com/2017/5/4/15548760/philadelphia-eagles-release-terrell-watson-josh-leribeus-andrew-bonnett |access-date=September 27, 2025 |website=Bleeding Green Nation|publisher=SB Nation}}</ref>

'''Andrew Adams''' (born October 28, 1992) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Connecticut Huskies football|Connecticut Huskies]].<ref name="UCONN" />

==College career==
Adams started 33 games throughout his college tenure including all 12 in 2014 and all 13 in 2015. He was one of four [[team captain|captains]] his senior year with the Huskies. He led the Huskies with 103 [[Tackle (football move)#Gridiron football|tackles]], as well as adding three [[interceptions]] and seven [[passes defended]] in his final season as a Husky.<ref name="UCONN">{{Cite web |title=22 – Andrew Adams |url=http://www.uconnhuskies.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/andrew_adams_763717.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180210180723/http://www.uconnhuskies.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/andrew_adams_763717.html |archive-date=February 10, 2018 |access-date=September 24, 2016 |website=www.uconnhuskies.com}}</ref>
