===New York Giants (first stint)===
====2016====
On May 1, 2016, the [[New York Giants]] signed Adams to a three-year, $1.62 million contract as an [[undrafted free agent]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eisen |first=Michael |date=May 6, 2016 |title=Giants sign four draft picks & 14 undrafted free agents |url=http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/Giants-sign-four-draft-picks--14-undrafted-free-agents/bce88848-ed81-4d6a-8e99-26f19049be9d |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170803005711/http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/Giants-sign-four-draft-picks--14-undrafted-free-agents/bce88848-ed81-4d6a-8e99-26f19049be9d |archive-date=August 3, 2017 |access-date=September 24, 2016 |website=Giants.com}}</ref><ref name="spotrac">{{Cite web |title=Spotrac.com: Andrew Adams contract |url=https://www.spotrac.com/nfl/new-york-giants/andrew-adam-19523/ |access-date=January 4, 2019 |website=Spotrac.com}}</ref>
[[file:Andrew Adams (American football).JPG|thumb|left|200px|Adams playing for the [[New York Giants]] in 2017.]]
On September 3, 2016, the Giants waived Adams as part of their final roster cuts, but signed him to their [[practice squad]] the following day.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eisen |first=Michael |date=September 3, 2016 |title=New York Giants announce 20 roster moves |url=http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/New-York-Giants-announce-20-roster-moves/d7b93d76-3186-40dc-b759-c622015e0159 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170825063500/http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/New-York-Giants-announce-20-roster-moves/d7b93d76-3186-40dc-b759-c622015e0159 |archive-date=August 25, 2017 |access-date=September 24, 2016 |website=Giants.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Eisen |first=Michael |date=September 4, 2016 |title=Giants announce practice squad; claim DT Robert Thomas |url=http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/Giants-announce-practice-squad-claim-DT-Robert-Thomas/e8402e2e-7f9b-4c94-95db-b9d10f79333e |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170909053715/http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/Giants-announce-practice-squad-claim-DT-Robert-Thomas/e8402e2e-7f9b-4c94-95db-b9d10f79333e |archive-date=September 9, 2017 |access-date=September 24, 2016 |website=Giants.com}}</ref> On September 23, 2016, Adams was promoted from practice squad to the active roster.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eisen |first=Michael |date=September 23, 2016 |title=Giants promote safety Andrew Adams |url=http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/Giants-promote-safety-Andrew-Adams/a70612d2-99f7-4444-bfcd-c54e0d20cc49 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160925143040/http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/Giants-promote-safety-Andrew-Adams/a70612d2-99f7-4444-bfcd-c54e0d20cc49 |archive-date=September 25, 2016 |access-date=September 24, 2016 |website=Giants.com}}</ref> On September 25, 2016, Adams made one tackle during a 29–27 loss against the [[Washington Redskins]] in Week 3. On October 3, 2016, Adams earned his first career start after starting [[free safety]] [[Darian Thompson]] suffered a foot injury and  backup [[Nat Berhe]] was inactive due to a concussion.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Estrict |first=Brandon |date=November 27, 2016 |title=Giants' Injury News: Mark Herzlich & Nat Berhe out (concussions) |url=https://www.bigblueview.com/giants-browns-2016-nfl-schedule-week-12-preview-final-score-recap-news-analysis/2016/11/27/13757764/ny-giants-injury-news-nat-berhe-concussion-odell-beckham-leaves-game |access-date=January 4, 2019 |website=bigblueview.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=September 30, 2016 |title=Giants rookie Andrew Adams ready to erase memory of costly penalty |url=https://www.nj.com/giants/index.ssf/2016/09/giants_rookie_andrew_adams_ready_to_erase_memory_o.html |access-date=January 4, 2019 |website=NJ.com}}</ref> He finished the Giants’ 24–10 loss at the [[Minnesota Vikings]] with six combined tackles and one pass deflection. On November 6, 2016, Adams collected a season-high nine combined tackles, deflected two passes, and made his first career interception during a 28–23 win against the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] in Week 9. Adams intercepted a pass by Eagles’ quarterback [[Carson Wentz]], that was initially intended for wide receiver [[Dorial Green-Beckham]], and returned it for a 19-yard gain in the first quarter.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Philadelphia Eagles at New York Giants – November 6th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201611060nyg.htm |access-date=March 16, 2021 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He finished his rookie season in 2016 with 46 combined tackles (31 solo), five pass deflections, and one interception in 14 games and 13 starts.<ref name="career">{{Cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Andrew Adams (career) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/andrewadams/2556456/careerstats |access-date=January 4, 2019 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> He received an overall grade of 79.4 from [[Pro Football Focus]], which was the second best grade among rookie safeties in 2016 behind [[Keanu Neal]] (80.8).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Raanan |first=Jordan |date=April 24, 2017 |title=Giants' Andrew Adams is latest example draft goes beyond Round 7 |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/new-york-giants/post/_/id/51548/giants-andrew-adams-the-latest-example-draft-extends-beyond-seven-rounds |access-date=January 4, 2019 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

====2017====
During [[Training camp (NFL)|training camp]], Adams competed to be a starting free safety against [[Darian Thompson]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Schneier |first=Dan |date=June 4, 2017 |title=Giants will have open competition for final safety spot |url=https://247sports.com/nfl/new-york-giants/article/darian-thompson-andrew-adams-new-york-giants-competition-at-safety-53073971/ |access-date=January 4, 2019 |website=247sports.com}}</ref> Head coach [[Ben McAdoo]] named Adams the backup free safety, behind Darian Thompson, to start the regular season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 9, 2017 |title=A look at the depth chart for the 2017 Giants |url=https://www.northjersey.com/story/sports/nfl/giants/2017/09/09/look-depth-chart-2017-giants/646540001/ |access-date=January 4, 2019 |website=northjersey.com}}</ref> In Week 17, he collected a season-high seven solo tackles and deflected a pass during a 18–10 win against the Redskins.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Andrew Adams (2017) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/andrewadams/2556456/gamelogs?season=2017 |access-date=January 4, 2019 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> On December 4, 2017, the New York Giants fired head coach Ben McAdoo after they fell to a 2–10 record.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Patra |first=Kevin |date=December 4, 2017 |title=New York Giants fire coach Ben McAdoo after 2–10 start |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/new-york-giants-fire-coach-ben-mcadoo-after-2-10-start-0ap3000000887801 |access-date=March 16, 2021 |website=NFL.com |language=en-US}}</ref> He finished the [[2017 NFL season]] with 34 solo tackles and two pass deflections in 16 games and four starts.<ref name="career" />

====2018====
During training camp, Adams competed against Darian Thompson to be the starting free safety.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 6, 2018 |title=Giants' Andrew Adams, Darian Thompson enjoying friendly competition |url=https://giantswire.usatoday.com/2018/07/06/new-york-giants-andrew-adams-darian-thompson-enjoying-friendly-competition/ |access-date=January 4, 2019 |website=giantswire.usatoday.com}}</ref>
On September 1, 2018, the New York Giants officially waived Adams.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eisen |first=Michael |date=September 1, 2018 |title=New York Giants announce 53-man roster |url=https://www.giants.com/news/new-york-giants-announce-53-man-roster |access-date=March 16, 2021 |website=Giants.com}}</ref>

===Tampa Bay Buccaneers (first stint)===
On September 26, 2018, the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] signed Adams after placing [[Chris Conte]] on [[injured reserve]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith, Scott |date=September 26, 2018 |title=Bucs Sign Safety Andrew Adams |url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/bucs-sign-safety-andrew-adams |website=Buccaneers.com}}</ref> Head coach [[Dirk Koetter]] named Adams the backup free safety behind [[Jordan Whitehead]]. On December 2, 2018, Adams made one tackle, three pass deflections, and made a career-high three interceptions during a 24–17 victory against the [[Carolina Panthers]].<ref name="w188">{{cite web | last=Adams | first=Bailey | title=Buccaneers vs. Panthers Recap: The Andrew Adams Show | website=Bucs Nation | date=2018-12-02 | url=https://www.bucsnation.com/2018/12/2/18121763/nfl-tampa-bay-buccaneers-vs-carolina-panthers-recap | access-date=2024-10-12}}</ref> In Week 15, Adams collected a season-high seven combined tackles and deflected a pass as the Buccaneers lost 27–20 at the [[Dallas Cowboys]]. He finished the season with 38 combined tackles (29 solo), nine pass deflections, and four interceptions in 13 games and four starts.<ref name="career" />

===Detroit Lions===
On March 14, 2019, Adams signed a one-year contract with the [[Detroit Lions]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 14, 2019 |title=Lions sign free agents OL Oday Aboushi and S Andrew Adams |url=https://www.detroitlions.com/news/lions-sign-free-agents-ol-oday-aboushi-and-s-andrew-adams |access-date=March 14, 2019 |website=Detroit Lions}}</ref> He was released during final roster cuts on August 30, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mullenax |first=Steven |title=Detroit Lions 2019 roster cuts tracker (updated) |url=https://sidelionreport.com/2019/08/30/detroit-lions-2019-roster-cuts-tracker-updated/ |access-date=August 30, 2019 |website=SideLionReport.com|date=August 30, 2019 }}</ref>

===Tampa Bay Buccaneers (second stint)===
[[File:Andrew Adams.png|thumb|Adams making a tackle in a game against the [[Tennessee Titans]] ]]
On September 10, 2019, Adams was signed by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith, Scott |date=September 10, 2019 |title=Justin Evans Lands on IR Amid Round of Roster Moves |url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/justin-evans-injured-reserve-andrew-adams-roster-moves |website=Buccaneers.com}}</ref>
In Week 8 against the [[Tennessee Titans]], Adams forced a [[fumble]] on [[Derrick Henry]] which was recovered by teammate [[Vernon Hargreaves]] in the 27–23 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 27, 2019 |title=Titans force 4 turnovers by Winston, hold off Tampa Bay |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401128048 |access-date=October 27, 2019 |website=[[ESPN]] |agency=Associated Press}}</ref>
In Week 15 against his former team, the Lions, Adams recorded his first interception of the season off rookie quarterback [[David Blough]] during the 38–17 win.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 15, 2019 |title=Winston throws 4 TDs, helps Buccaneers beat Lions 38–17 |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401128028 |access-date=December 15, 2019 |website=[[ESPN]] |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> Overall, in the 2019 season, Adams recorded 45 total tackles, one interception, one forced fumble and three passes defensed in 14 games.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andrew Adams 2019 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/A/AdamAn00/gamelog/2019/ |access-date=March 16, 2021 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

On March 24, 2020, Adams was re-signed to a one-year, $1 million contract.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Scott |date=March 24, 2020 |title=Bucs Re-Sign Two More Defenders |url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/bucs-re-sign-andrew-adams-rakeem-nunez-roches-free-agency-roster-move |access-date=March 16, 2021 |website=Buccaneers.com}}</ref> Adams played in all four games in the Buccaneers' playoff run that resulted in the team winning [[Super Bowl LV]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Patra |first=Kevin |date=February 7, 2017 |title=What we learned from Buccaneers win over Chiefs in Super Bowl LV |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/what-we-learned-from-buccaneers-win-over-chiefs-in-super-bowl-lv |access-date=March 16, 2021 |website=NFL.com |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Super Bowl LV – Tampa Bay Buccaneers vs. Kansas City Chiefs – February 7th, 2021 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202102070tam.htm |access-date=March 16, 2021 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Andrew Adams 2020 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/A/AdamAn00/gamelog/2020/ |access-date=March 16, 2021 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Philadelphia Eagles===
On March 18, 2021, Adams signed a one-year contract with the [[Philadelphia Eagles]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Eagles agree to terms with S Andrew Adams|url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-agree-to-terms-with-andrew-adams|author=McPherson, Chris|website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com|date=March 18, 2021}}</ref> He was waived on August 31.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Kempski|first=Jimmy|date=August 31, 2021|title=Eagles announce initial 53-man roster, with analysis|url=https://www.phillyvoice.com/eagles-announce-initial-53-man-roster-analysis-2021/|url-status=live|access-date=|website=PhillyVoice|language=english|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210831220133/https://www.phillyvoice.com/eagles-announce-initial-53-man-roster-analysis-2021/ |archive-date=August 31, 2021 }}</ref>

===Tampa Bay Buccaneers (third stint)===
On September 2, 2021, Adams rejoined the Buccaneers as a member of their practice squad<ref>{{cite web|title=Bucs Activate Ryan Succop, Add to Practice Squad|url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/bucs-activate-ryan-succop-practice-squad-signings-roster-moves|author=Smith, Scott|website=Buccaneers.com|date=September 2, 2021}}</ref> and was signed to the active roster on September 13.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bucs Promote Andrew Adams, Put Two on IR|url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/bucs-promote-andrew-adams-place-two-injured-reserve-roster-moves|author=Smith, Scott|website=Buccaneers.com|date=September 13, 2021}}</ref> He was hit on his helmet by his Coach [[Bruce Arians]] after their 31 - 15 playoff win.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/nfl-fines-buccaneers-head-coach-bruce-arians-50-000-for-striking-player-on-helme|title=NFL fines Buccaneers head coach Bruce Arians $50,000 for striking player on helmet|website=[[NFL.com]]}}</ref> He was trying to pull a player out of a scrum, Bruce later said, "No, I've seen enough dumb (things). You can't pull guys out of a pile. We just got a big play, great field position, and he's trying to pull a guy out of a pile."<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-01-20 |title=Bruce Arians Fined $50,000 For Slapping One Of His Buccaneers Players |url=https://www.inquisitr.com/6501570/bruce-arians-fined-50000-for-slapping-one-of-his-buccaneers-pla |access-date=2022-08-31 |website=The Inquisitr}}</ref>

===New York Giants (second stint)===
On July 26, 2022, the Giants signed Adams.<ref>{{cite web|title=Giants sign 4 players ahead of training camp|url=https://www.giants.com/news/roster-transactions-andrew-adams-marcus-kemp-nicholas-williams-kamaal-seymour|author=Eisen, Michael|website=Giants.com|date=July 26, 2022|access-date=July 26, 2022|archive-date=July 26, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220726152523/https://www.giants.com/news/roster-transactions-andrew-adams-marcus-kemp-nicholas-williams-kamaal-seymour|url-status=dead}}</ref> On August 26, 2022, he was released.<ref name="m111">{{cite web | last=Eisen | first=Michael | title=Giants sign K Ryan Santoso, WR Travis Toivonen; DB Andrew Adams released | website=Giants.com| date=2022-08-26 | url=https://www.giants.com/news/ryan-santoso-travis-toivonen-andrew-adams-roster-moves-training-camp-2022 | access-date=2024-12-03}}</ref>

===Pittsburgh Steelers===
On September 5, 2022, Adams was signed to the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Steelers sign three to practice squad|url=https://www.steelers.com/news/steelers-sign-three-to-practice-squad|author=Varley, Teresa|website=Steelers.com|date=September 5, 2022}}</ref>

===Tennessee Titans===
On September 21, 2022, Adams was signed by the [[Tennessee Titans]] off the Steelers practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Titans Add DBs Terrance Mitchell, Andrew Adams to 53-Man Roster, Place Two Others on Injured Reserve|url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-add-dbs-terrance-mitchell-andrew-adams-to-53-man-roster-place-two-others-|author=Wyatt, Jim|website=TennesseeTitans.com|date=September 21, 2022}}</ref> Adams returned an interception from quarterback [[Matt Ryan (American football)|Matt Ryan]] for his first career defensive [[touchdown]] in a 19–10 Week 7 win over the [[Indianapolis Colts]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Titans Sweep Colts for the Second Year in a Row, Thanks to Sunday's 19-10 Win|url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-sweep-colts-for-the-second-year-in-a-row-thanks-to-sunday-s-19-10-win|author=Wyatt, Jim|website=TennesseeTitans.com|date=October 23, 2022|access-date=October 23, 2022}}</ref> On January 2, 2023, Adams was placed on season–ending injured reserve after suffering a torn [[patellar tendon]] in Week 17 against the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]].<ref name="q240">{{cite web | last=Moraitis | first=Mike | title=Titans place Andrew Adams on IR among 3 moves | website=Titans Wire|publisher=USA Today | date=2023-01-02 | url=https://titanswire.usatoday.com/2023/01/02/tennessee-titans-andrew-adams-injured-reserve-mike-brown-browns/ | access-date=2024-12-03}}</ref>

===Baltimore Ravens===
On October 17, 2023, the [[Baltimore Ravens]] signed Adams to their practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brown |first=Clifton |date=18 October 2023 |title=Reports: Ravens to Sign Veteran Safety to Practice Squad |url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/reports-ravens-sign-andrew-adams-safety-practice-squad-week-7 |access-date=18 October 2023 |website=Ravens Wire|publisher=USA Today}}</ref> He was not signed to a reserve/future contract after the season and thus became a free agent when his practice squad contract expired.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/ravens-sign-nine-players-reserve-future-deals-contract|publisher=[[Baltimore Ravens]]|title=Ravens Sign 10 Players to Reserve/Future Deals |date=January 29, 2024|author=Mink, Ryan}}</ref>

{{Short description|Danish-born American football player (born 1991)}} {{Use mdy dates|date=January 2019}} {{Infobox NFL biography | name = Andreas Knappe | image = | caption = | number = 73 | position = [[Offensive tackle]] | birth_date = {{birth date and age|mf=yes|1991|6|2}} | birth_place = [[Silkeborg]], Denmark | height_ft = 6 | height_in = 8 | weight_lbs = 325 | high_school = Handelsskolen Silkeborg
(Silkeborg, Denmark) | college = [[Connecticut Huskies football|Connecticut]] | undraftedyear = 2017 | pastteams = * [[Atlanta Falcons]] ({{NFL Year|2017}})* * [[Washington Redskins]] ({{NFL Year|2017}})* * [[Indianapolis Colts]] ({{NFL Year|2017}})* * [[Denver Broncos]] ({{NFL Year|2018|2019}})* | pfr = KnapAn00 }} '''Andreas Emil Knappe''' (born June 2, 1991) is a [[Danes|Danish]]-born former [[American football]] [[offensive tackle]]. He played [[college football]] at the [[Connecticut Huskies football|University of Connecticut]]. He was the first Danish player to sign with an NFL team since [[placekicker|kicker]] [[Morten Andersen]].{{Cite news |url=http://www.americanfootballinternational.com/andreas-knappe-signs-atlanta-falcons-1st-dane-nfl-since-morten-andersen/ |title=Andreas Knappe signs with Atlanta Falcons; 1st Dane in NFL since Morten Andersen |date=April 30, 2017 |work=American Football International |access-date=November 23, 2018 |language=en-US}} ==Early life== Knappe grew up in [[Silkeborg, Denmark]] and played [[team handball]] as a youth. He was also an archer on the Danish national team, but got tired of it. Knappe first began playing football at the age of 18 because a friend recommended it. After playing for a local team, Knappe joined football powerhouse Triangle Razorbacks of the [[Danish American Football Federation]]. He competed on the defensive line on the team that won the 2011 Mermaid Bowl.{{cite news |title=It's a brave new world for UConn lineman Andreas Knappe |url=https://www.nhregister.com/uconn/article/It-s-a-brave-new-world-for-UConn-lineman-11341189.php |access-date=February 18, 2020 |work=[[New Haven Register]] |date=August 29, 2015}} In 2012, he came to the United States to attend some football camps, and attracted the attention of coach [[Paul Pasqualoni]] at the [[University of Connecticut]].{{cite news |title=Danish archer becomes football star for UConn |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/44427064/danish_archer_becomes_football_star_for/ |access-date=February 18, 2020 |work=[[Grand Junction Daily Sentinel|The Daily Sentinel]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=August 9, 2015 |page=18|via=Newspapers.com}} ==College career== Knappe redshirted his first season at [[UConn Huskies football|UConn]], playing on the defensive line. He played in one game in 2013. In 2014 he played in 10 games, starting the final seven of the season at right tackle. After the season he was named to the 2014 American Athletic Conference All-Academic team. He started all 25 games his final two seasons.{{cite news |last1=Culpepper |first1=JuliaKate |title=Falcons' Andreas Knappe dreamed of being an Olympic archer |url=https://www.ajc.com/sports/falcons-andreas-knappe-dreamed-being-olympic-archer/EF6qow0x5hBc6nl1O6XyDL/ |access-date=February 18, 2020 |work=[[Atlanta Journal-Constitution]] |date=May 12, 2017}} Knappe participated in the Goal Line Project, a charity in which he mentored inner-city middle school kids. He was on the 2015 watchlist for the Wuerffel Trophy, awarded to the best FBS player who combines community service with athletic achievement. ==Professional career== ===Atlanta Falcons=== Knappe signed with the [[Atlanta Falcons]] as an undrafted free agent on May 1, 2017.{{cite web|title=Falcons Agree To Terms With 21 CFAs|url=http://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/blog/article-1/Falcons-Agree-to-Terms-With-21-CFAs/1dbd9631-8b92-4405-8d9b-71fa59a85946|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171014031455/http://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/blog/article-1/Falcons-Agree-to-Terms-With-21-CFAs/1dbd9631-8b92-4405-8d9b-71fa59a85946|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 14, 2017|author=Jackson, Curtis|website=AtlantaFalcons.com|date=May 1, 2017|access-date=January 30, 2018}} He was waived by the Falcons on September 2, 2017.{{cite web|title=2017 Atlanta Falcons Roster Cuts Tracker: Deadline To 53 Is 4 P.M. '''Andre Smith Jr.''' (born April 20, 1997) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[linebacker]]. He played [[college football]] at [[North Carolina Tar Heels football|North Carolina]].

==Early life==
Smith attended Trinity Christian Academy in [[Jacksonville, Florida]]. As a senior, he tallied 65 [[tackled gridiron|tackles]] with 5.5 being for loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andre Smith |url=http://www.goheels.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=12519 |access-date=December 31, 2017 |publisher=University of North Carolina Tar Heels Official Athletic Site}}</ref> He committed to play football for the [[North Carolina Tar Heels]] in October 2013.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Smith Is UNC Commit No. 2 for 2015 |url=https://247sports.com/college/north-carolina/article/2015-lb-andre-smith-talks-commitment-to-unc-155140/ |access-date=December 31, 2017 |publisher=Carolina Blue}}</ref>

==College career==
As a [[true freshman]] in 2015, Smith played in all of North Carolina's 14 games. He tallied 53 tackles, two being for losses, one [[interception]], one pass breakup, and one forced [[fumble]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andre Smith 2015 Player Statistics |url=http://www.cfbstats.com/2015/player/457/1071686/index.html |access-date=December 31, 2017 |publisher=cfbstats}}</ref>

In 2016, Smith played in all 13 games, starting 12 of them at middle [[linebacker]]. He made 113 tackles, second on the team, along with one interception, one [[qb sack|sack]], three pass deflections, and one forced fumble.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andre Smith 2016 Player Statistics |url=http://www.cfbstats.com/2016/player/457/1071686/index.html |access-date=December 31, 2017 |publisher=cfbstats}}</ref>

As a junior in 2017, Smith suffered a knee injury in North Carolina's second game against Louisville, forcing him to miss the remainder of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andre Smith, UNC's star linebacker, is out for the season. Here's who will replace him. |url=http://www.newsobserver.com/sports/college/acc/unc/article174834131.html |access-date=December 31, 2017 |publisher=The News & Observer}}</ref> In only two games, he tallied 21 tackles and a 73 yard interception return.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andre Smith 2017 Player Statistics |url=http://www.cfbstats.com/2017/player/457/1071686/index.html |access-date=December 31, 2017 |publisher=cfbstats}}</ref> After the season, he declared for the [[2018 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=UNC linebacker Andre Smith to enter NFL draft |url=http://www.heraldsun.com/sports/college/acc/unc/article192371614.html |access-date=December 31, 2017 |publisher=The Herald Sun}}</ref>

'''Andrew Jelks''' (born December 6, 1993) is an American former [[American football|football]] [[offensive tackle]]. He played college football at [[Vanderbilt University]], and was signed by the [[New England Patriots]] as an undrafted free agent after the [[2017 NFL draft]].

==College career==
Jelks played in 24 games with 21 starts at [[Vanderbilt Commodores football|Vanderbilt]] over the course of five seasons. Jelks missed his final two seasons in 2015 and 2016 due to injuries. He began his career at right tackle and moved to left tackle as a sophomore.

==Professional career==
===New England Patriots===
Jelks was signed by the [[New England Patriots]] as an undrafted free agent on May 5, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Patriots Sign Sixth-Round Draft Pick Conor McDermott; Sign 19 Rookie Free Agents|url=https://www.patriots.com/news/patriots-sign-sixth-round-draft-pick-conor-mcdermott-sign-19-rookie-free--298276|website=Patriots.com|date=May 5, 2017|accessdate=June 4, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170512003817/http://www.patriots.com/news/2017/05/05/patriots-sign-sixth-round-draft-pick-conor-mcdermott-sign-19-rookie-free-agents|archive-date=2017-05-12|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was placed on reserve/non-football injury list prior to the start of the season due to a torn ACL suffered during pre-season workouts his senior year at Vanderbilt, and would remain on the list for the entire 2017 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.patspulpit.com/2017/12/1/16713046/new-england-patriots-rookie-offensive-tackle-andrew-jelks-vanderbilt-non-football-injury-list|title=Patriots OT Andrew Jelks to miss third straight season after not getting activated off NFI|website=PatsPulpit|date=December 2017 |access-date=April 1, 2018}}</ref>

===Retirement===
Jelks announced his retirement on July 19, 2018.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://247sports.com/nfl/new-england-patriots/Article/Andrew-Jelks-retires-from-the-NFL-119968038/|title=Andrew Jelks retires from the NFL|website=247sports.com|date=July 19, 2018|access-date=July 21, 2018}}</ref>

'''Andre Eric Szmyt''' ({{IPAc-en|ʃ|m|ɪ|t}} {{respell|SHMIT}};<ref>[https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-sign-k-andre-szmyt "Browns sign K Andre Szmyt," ClevelandBrowns.com, Thursday 26 June 2025.] Retrieved 14 September 2025.</ref> born September 26, 1998) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[placekicker]] for the [[Cleveland Browns]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Syracuse Orange football|Syracuse Orange]].

==College career==
Szmyt [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]] his true freshman year in 2017, and was named to the SU Athletic Director’s Honor Roll in the fall.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andre Szmyt - Football |url=https://cuse.com/sports/football/roster/andre-szmyt/21447 |access-date=2025-10-31 |website=Syracuse University Athletics |language=en}}</ref>

In 2018, Szmyt became the first Syracuse kicker and third freshman to win the [[Lou Groza Award]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://theacc.com/news/2018/12/6/football-syracuses-szmyt-wins-groza-award.aspx |title=SYRACUSE'S SZMYT WINS GROZA AWARD |date=December 6, 2018 |publisher=[[Atlantic Coast Conference]] |access-date=December 15, 2018}}</ref> and was named a [[unanimous All-American]], being the first since [[Dwight Freeney]] in 2001.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cuse.com/news/2018/12/12/football-szmyt-a-unanimous-all-american.aspx|title=SZMYT A UNANIMOUS ALL-AMERICAN|publisher=[[Syracuse Orange|Syracuse University Athletic Department]] |date=December 12, 2018}}</ref> Szmyt also won the 2018 [[Touchdown Club of Columbus#Vlade Award|Vlade Award]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaaf/2018/12/04/syracuse-place-kicker-andre-szmyt-wins-vlade-award/38670487/|title=Syracuse place-kicker Andre Szmyt wins Vlade Award|date=December 4, 2018|publisher=[[USA Today]]}}</ref> In 2018, Szmyt connected on 30 of 34 field goals, and hit all 61 extra points. He also kicked a season-high 54 yard field goal in a loss to Pittsburgh.

In the 2019 season, Szmyt was successful on 17 of 20 field goals, one of which was a 50 yard field goal in the beginning of the second quarter in a loss at [[2019 Florida State Seminoles football team|Florida State.]] Against Wake Forest on the last week of the season, he connected on a 49 yard field goal with 44 seconds left until the Demon Deacons tied the game. In overtime he also kicked a 40 yard field goal in the 39-30 win (Syracuse got the score off a fumble return touchdown).

In the 2020 season, Szmyt successfully completed 9 of 11 field goal attempts in a shortened season.

In the 2021 season, Szmyt only successfully completed 9 of 14 field goal attempts.

Szmyt's performance was marred by coaching changes and his holders switching, but he returned to a better form when [[Bob Ligashesky]] took over as the [[special teams]] coordinator in 2022.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Alandt |first1=Anthony |title=A kicking camp, Bob Ligashesky helped Andre Szmyt return to 'old Andre' |url=https://dailyorange.com/2022/10/andre-szmyt-return-to-old-form/ |access-date=October 13, 2022 |work=[[The Daily Orange]] |date=October 13, 2022}}</ref> That season, he connected on 20 of 26 field goals and all 40 of his extra point attempts.

'''Andrew Monroe Davison''' (December 9, 1979 – February 7, 2017) was an American professional [[American football|football]] [[cornerback]] in the [[National Football League]] for the [[New York Jets]] and [[Dallas Cowboys]]. He played [[college football]] at the [[University of Kansas]].

==Early life==
Davison initially attended [[Cody High School (Detroit, Michigan)|Cody High School]], but was expelled as a freshman because of his conduct. He transferred to [[Chadsey High School]], where he began playing football.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article132964454.html | title=Words to live by: KU's Andrew Davison says tough talk is a reflection of his past | access-date=January 12, 2019}}</ref>

He was a two-way player at [[cornerback]] and [[wide receiver]]. As a senior, he posted 45 tackles, 7 interceptions, 2 fumble recoveries, 48 receptions for 716 yards and 11 touchdowns, while receiving All-Detroit honors. He played on the Shrine High School All-star game.

He also was a sprinter on the [[track & field|track]] team.

==College career==
Davison accepted a football scholarship from the [[University of Kansas]]. As a true freshman, he started four-of-nine games at [[cornerback]], making 21 tackles. He was known to be one of the most outspoken players on the team.

As a sophomore, he became a full-time starter, posting 53 tackles, 5 passes defensed, 2 forced fumbles and one interception (returned for a [[touchdown]]). As a junior, he had one interception (returned for a 40-yard [[touchdown]]) and 9 passes defensed.

As a senior, he led the team with 3 interceptions and 12 pass breakups. He was a four-year starter (38-of-43 games), recording 176 tackles, 6 interceptions (2 returned for [[touchdown]]s) and 27 passes defensed.

==Professional career==
===New York Jets (first stint)===
Davison was signed as an [[undrafted free agent]] by the [[New York Jets]] after the [[2002 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.nytimes.com/2002/08/19/sports/pro-football-a-nervous-jets-rookie-finds-some-tranquillity.html | title=A Nervous Jets Rookie Finds Some Tranquillity | access-date=January 12, 2019}}</ref> As a rookie, he was a backup [[cornerback]], registering 5 defensive tackles and 6 [[special teams]] tackles.

In [[2003 NFL season|2003]], he sprained his left ankle in the preseason finale against the [[Philadelphia Eagles]]. He was waived with an injury settlement on August 31.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.nytimes.com/2003/09/01/sports/pro-football-pennington-says-he-will-miss-9-games.html | title=Pennington Says He Will Miss 9 Games | access-date=January 12, 2019}}</ref>

===Dallas Cowboys===
On September 18, [[2003 NFL season|2003]], he was signed as a [[free agent]] by the [[Dallas Cowboys]] to provide depth.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.nytimes.com/2003/09/19/sports/transactions-355151.html | title=Transactions | access-date=January 12, 2019}}</ref> He was declared inactive for 10 games, until making his debut in the thirteenth game against the [[Philadelphia Eagles]]. He played mostly on [[special teams]]. In the season finale against the [[New Orleans Saints]], he played on the dime package, but suffered a sprained medial collateral ligament in his right knee. On January 1, he was placed on the [[injured reserve list]], forcing him to miss the Wild Card playoff game against the [[Carolina Panthers]].<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.nytimes.com/2004/01/02/sports/transactions-805386.html | title=Transactions | access-date=January 12, 2019}}</ref> He had one [[special teams]] tackle.

On August 9, [[2004 NFL season|2004]], it was reported in the media that he left the team on his own during [[Training camp (National Football League)|training camp]].<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.newspapers.com/newspage/331708238/ | title=Extra Points| access-date=January 12, 2019}}</ref>

===New York Jets (second stint)===
On August 16, [[2004 NFL season|2004]], he was signed by the [[New York Jets]] as a [[free agent]].<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.nytimes.com/2004/08/17/sports/transactions-660884.html | title=Transactions | access-date=January 12, 2019}}</ref> He was released on September 5.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.nytimes.com/2004/09/06/sports/football/jets-cuts-include-four-former-draft-picks.html | title=Jets' Cuts Include Four Former Draft Picks | access-date=January 12, 2019}}</ref> He was signed to the [[practice squad]] on September 6.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.nytimes.com/2004/09/07/sports/transactions.html | title=Transactions | access-date=January 12, 2019}}</ref>

On January 24, [[2005 NFL season|2005]], he was signed by the [[New York Jets]].<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.nytimes.com/2005/01/25/sports/transactions.html | title=Transactions | access-date=January 12, 2019}}</ref> He was released on June 2.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.newspapers.com/newspage/125576800/ | title=Transactions | access-date=January 12, 2019}}</ref>

==Personal life==
On February 7, 2017, he died after battling a heart condition for six years.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/former-jets-cowboys-cb-andrew-davison-dies-at-age-37/ | title=Former Jets, Cowboys CB Andrew Davison dies at age 37 | access-date=January 12, 2019}}</ref> After his junior season in college, he was a victim of a [[drive-by shooting]], that left him with a bullet fragment lodged in his arm.

'''Andrew Beck''' (born May 15, 1996) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Fullback (gridiron football)|fullback]] for the [[New York Jets]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Texas Longhorns football|Texas Longhorns]]. 

==Early life==
Beck attended and played [[high school football]] at [[Henry B. Plant High School]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andrew Beck, Plant, Inside Linebacker |url=https://247sports.com/Player/Andrew-Beck-24226/high-school-38801/ |access-date=January 2, 2020 |website=247Sports |language=en-US}}</ref>

==College career==
Beck was a member of the [[Texas Longhorns football|Texas Longhorns]] football team for five seasons. He became a starter at [[tight end]] and [[H-back]] for the team as a sophomore, catching eight passes for 77 yards while serving primarily as a blocker.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eberts |first=Wescott |date=April 28, 2016 |title=Texas H-back Andrew Beck working to elevate his game |url=https://www.burntorangenation.com/2016/4/28/11521894/andrew-beck-texas-longhorns-spring-football |access-date=September 5, 2019 |website=BurntOrangeNation.com |publisher=SB Nation}}</ref> In his junior season, Beck caught four passes for 82 yards and two [[touchdowns]] while blocking for the nation's leading rusher, [[D'Onta Foreman]]. He missed the entirety of his senior season and was forced to use a medical [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]] after breaking his foot in a preseason practice.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Carlton |first=Chuck |date=August 16, 2017 |title=Longhorns down another TE after senior Andrew Beck fractures foot in practice |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/texas-longhorns/2017/08/17/longhorns-down-another-te-after-senior-andrew-beck-fractures-foot-in-practice/ |access-date=September 5, 2019 |website=[[The Dallas Morning News]]}}</ref> As a redshirt senior, Beck had 28 [[football catch|receptions]] for 281 yards and two touchdowns and was named first-team All-[[Big 12 Conference]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Weinrib |first=Ben |date=May 5, 2019 |title=Patriots spend big on UDFA who could fill Rob Gronkowski's role |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/patriots-replacement-gronk-andrew-beck-190554045.html |access-date=September 5, 2019 |website=[[Yahoo Sports]]}}</ref>

===New England Patriots===
Beck signed with the [[New England Patriots]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] on May 4, 2019, after agreeing to a guaranteed salary of $115,000, making him the highest paid undrafted signing by the team.<ref>{{Cite web |last=DePrisco |first=Michael |date=May 4, 2019 |title=Report: Patriots make Texas TE Andrew Beck highest paid UDFA |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/boston/patriots/report-patriots-make-texas-te-andrew-beck-highest-paid-udfa |access-date=September 4, 2019 |website=[[NBC Sports Boston]]}}</ref> The Patriots moved Beck to the [[fullback (gridiron football)|fullback]] position at the start of [[training camp (NFL)|training camp]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kyed |first=Doug |date=August 7, 2019 |title=Andrew Beck Could Add Jolt Of Athleticism To Patriots' Fullback Position |url=https://nesn.com/2019/08/andrew-beck-could-add-jolt-of-athleticism-to-patriots-fullback-position/ |access-date=September 4, 2019 |website=[[New England Sports Network|NESN.com]]}}</ref> He was waived during final roster cuts on August 30, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Thomas |first=Oliver |date=August 30, 2019 |title=Patriots roster cuts: New England waiving undrafted rookies Andrew Beck, Tyree St. Louis |url=https://www.patspulpit.com/2019/8/30/20840968/2019-nfl-new-england-patriots-roster-cuts-rookies-andrew-beck-tyree-st-louis-waived |access-date=September 4, 2019 |website=PatsPulpit.com |publisher=[[SB Nation]]}}</ref>

===Denver Broncos===
Beck was claimed off waivers by the [[Denver Broncos]] on September 1, 2019, to serve as the team's fullback after an injury to starter [[Andy Janovich]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Renck |first=Troy |date=September 1, 2019 |title=Broncos make flurry of waiver-wire claims, adding QB Brandon Allen, TE Andrew Beck |url=https://www.thedenverchannel.com/sports/broncos/broncos-make-flurry-of-waiver-wire-claims-adding-qb-brandon-allen-te-andrew-beck |access-date=September 4, 2019 |website=[[KMGH-TV|TheDenverChannel.com]]}}</ref> Beck made his NFL debut in the Broncos season opener of September 9, against the [[Oakland Raiders]]. He made his first career start on September 22, 2019, against the [[Green Bay Packers]], playing 23 snaps at fullback.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andrew Beck 2019 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BeckAn01/gamelog/2019/ |access-date=September 23, 2019 |website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]}}</ref> Beck caught a one-yard pass from [[Drew Lock]] for his first career touchdown on December 29, 2019, in a 16–15 win over the Raiders.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Linton |first=Chance |date=December 29, 2019 |title=Andrew Beck catches first career touchdown pass |url=https://247sports.com/Article/Denver-Broncos-Andrew-Beck-scores-first-career-touchdown-141276761/ |access-date=January 13, 2020 |website=247Sports.com}}</ref> He finished the 2019 season with 9 catches on 12 passes for 90 yards and a TD and 1 rush for 3 yards. He also threw 1 pass for 6 yards.

Beck was placed on the reserve/[[COVID-19]] list by the Broncos on July 30, 2020.<ref>{{Cite news |last=DiLalla, Aric |date=July 30, 2020 |title=Broncos place FB/TE Andrew Beck on Reserve/COVID-19 list |work=DenverBroncos.com |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-place-fb-te-andrew-beck-on-reserve-covid-19-list |access-date=July 30, 2020}}</ref> He was activated on August 17, 2020.<ref>{{Cite news |last=DiLalla, Aric |date=August 17, 2020 |title=Broncos activate FB/TE Andrew Beck from Reserve/COVID-19 list |work=DenverBroncos.com |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-activate-fb-te-andrew-beck-from-reserve-covid-19-list |access-date=August 18, 2020}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve on October 31 with a hamstring injury.<ref>{{Cite web |last=DiLalla, Aric |date=October 31, 2020 |title=Broncos activate LB Austin Calitro, promote RB Jeremy Cox to active roster |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-activate-lb-austin-calitro-promote-rb-jeremy-cox-to-active-roster |website=DenverBroncos.com}}</ref> He was activated on December 5, 2020.<ref>{{Cite news |last=DiLalla, Aric |date=December 5, 2020 |title=Broncos activate FB/TE Andrew Beck from IR |work=DenverBroncos.com |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-activate-fb-te-andrew-beck-from-ir |access-date=January 10, 2021 |archive-date=December 5, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201205221029/https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-activate-fb-te-andrew-beck-from-ir |url-status=dead }}</ref> He played in 10 games that season, but almost entirely on special teams, recording no stats.

On December 21, 2021, Beck was placed on injured reserve.<ref>{{Cite web |last=DiLalla, Aric |date=December 21, 2021 |title=Broncos activate RB Mike Boone from Reserve/COVID-19 list, place FB/TE Andrew Beck on IR |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-activate-rb-mike-boone-from-reserve-covid-19-list-place-fb-te-andrew-bec |website=DenverBroncos.com}}</ref>
On February 10, 2022, Beck was awarded the NFL's [[Salute to Service award]], presented by USAA annually.<ref name="c375">{{cite web | title=List of 'NFL Honors' award winners from 2021 NFL season | website=NFL.com | date=February 11, 2022 | url=https://www.nfl.com/news/list-of-nfl-honors-award-winners-from-2021-nfl-season | access-date=September 24, 2024}}</ref> In 2012, he played in 12 games, again almost entirely on special teams, recording just one solo tackle.

On March 14, 2022, Beck signed a one-year contract extension with the Broncos.<ref>{{Cite web |last=DiLalla |first=Aric |date=March 14, 2022 |title=Broncos sign FB/TE Andrew Beck to one-year contract |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-sign-fb-te-andrew-beck-to-one-year-contract |access-date=January 29, 2023 |website=DenverBroncos.com}}</ref> in 2022, he played in 13 games and filled in on offense in several games due to an injury to tight end [[Greg Dulcich]], recording 5 catches on 11 passes for 69 yards, 2 rushes and a tackle. He had his first four career starts that year. At the end of the season he became a free agent.

===Houston Texans (first stint)===
On March 17, 2023, Beck signed a two-year contract with the [[Houston Texans]], who moved him from tight end to fullback.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/houston-texans-transactions-3-17-2023|title=Houston Texans Transactions (3-17-2023)|last= |first= |date=March 17, 2023 |website=www.houstontexans.com|publisher=Houston Texans Public Relations|access-date=March 17, 2023}}</ref>

In 2023, he played in 15 games of which he started 12. He had 11 catches on 13 passes for 55 yards and 5 rushes for 3 yards and a touchdown. He also started in both of the Texans playoff games that year.

On September 24, 2023, in a game against the [[2023 Jacksonville Jaguars season|Jacksonville Jaguars]], Beck muffed a kickoff, but managed to return it for an 85-yard touchdown. The Texans won the game 37–17.<ref name="k457">{{cite web | last=Williams | first=Charean | title=Texans FB Andrew Beck returns kickoff 85 yards for TD, 24–10 lead | website=NBC Sports | date=September 24, 2023 | url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/texans-fb-andrew-beck-returns-kickoff-85-yards-for-td-24-10-lead | access-date=September 24, 2024}}</ref>
[[File:JBSA, AAFES NFL Youth Football Camp (23).jpg|thumb|right|250px|Beck (left) giving away an autographed Texans helmet in 2024]]
On January 6, 2024, in the final game of the regular season against the [[2023 Indianapolis Colts season|Indianapolis Colts]], Beck caught a 1-yard touchdown pass from [[C. J. Stroud]]. The Texans won the game 23–19, and clinched a playoff berth for the first time since [[2019 Houston Texans season|2019]].<ref name="q526">{{cite web | last=Kahler | first=Kalyn | last2=Boyd | first2=James | title=Texans punch postseason ticket after Colts' comeback falls short: Which key plays made the difference? | website=The New York Times | date=January 7, 2024 | url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5183537/2024/01/07/texans-colts-result-takeaways-week-18/ | access-date=December 27, 2024}}</ref>

Beck was placed on the Active/[[Physically Unable to Perform]] (PUP) list on July 18, 2024, and reactivated on July 29.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Houston Texans Transactions (07-18-2024) |url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/houston-texans-transactions-07-18-2024 |access-date=July 18, 2024 |website=HoustonTexans.com |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Ulrich |first1=Logan |title=Texans Activate FB Andrew Beck |url=https://nfltraderumors.co/texans-activate-fb-andrew-beck/ |access-date=December 3, 2024 |date=July 29, 2024}}</ref>

On August 27, 2024, Beck was released by the Texans when they cut to their initial 53-man roster.<ref>{{cite web|title=Houston Texans Transactions (08-27-2024)|url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/houston-texans-transactions-08-27-2024|website=HoustonTexans.com|date=August 27, 2024}}</ref>

===Green Bay Packers===
Beck was signed by the [[Green Bay Packers]] to their practice squad on August 30, 2024.<ref>{{cite web|title=Packers announce roster moves|url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-announce-roster-moves-aug-30-2024|website=Packers.com|date=August 30, 2024}}</ref> In October, he was elevated to the active roster for Weeks 5, 6 and 7.<ref>{{cite web|title=Packers announce roster moves|url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-announce-roster-moves-oct-5-2024|website=Packers.com|date=October 5, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Packers elevate FB Andrew Beck for gameday |url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-elevate-fb-andrew-beck-for-gameday-week-6-2024|website=Packers.com|date=October 12, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Packers elevate FB Andrew Beck for gameday|url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-elevate-fb-andrew-beck-for-gameday-week-7-2024|website=Packers.com|date=October 19, 2024}}</ref> The Packers released Beck from the practice squad on October 22, 2024, because he'd exhausted his special teams call-up allotment.<ref>{{cite web|title=Packers announce roster moves|url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-announce-roster-move-oct-22-2024|website=Packers.com|date=October 22, 2024}}</ref> Beck played in three games for the Packers and recorded 15 offensive snaps and 16 special teams snaps.<ref>{{cite web |title=Andrew Beck |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BeckAn01.htm |access-date=December 3, 2024}}</ref> He was targeted once as a receiver.

===Houston Texans (second stint)===
On November 28, 2024, Beck was signed to the Houston Texans practice squad.<ref>{{cite web |date=November 28, 2024 |title=Houston Texans Transactions (11-28-2024) |url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/houston-texans-transactions-11-28-2024 |access-date=March 5, 2026 |website=HoustonTexans.com}}</ref> Beck was elevated from the practice squad for one regular season game and played 12 snaps on offense during the game. He was targeted once as a receiver.

===New York Jets===
On February 7, 2025, Beck signed with the [[New York Jets]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets Sign FB Andrew Beck to Reserve/Future Deal|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-sign-andrew-beck-reserve-future-02-07-2025|author=Greenberg, Ethan|website=NewYorkJets.com|date=February 7, 2025}}</ref> After playing all 17 games in 2025, he re-signed with the team on March 12, 2026.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets Re-Sign FB Andrew Beck|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-re-sign-fullback-andrew-beck-free-agency-03-12-2026|author=Allen, Eric|website=NewYorkJets.com|date=March 12, 2026}}</ref>

Scouting assistant}} '''Andrew Dowell''' (born November 16, 1996) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] [[linebacker]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Michigan State Spartans football|Michigan State Spartans]]. He is current a scouting assistant for the [[Washington Commanders]] of the [[National Football League]]. ==Early life== Dowell attended [[St. Edward High School (Ohio)|St. Edward High School]]. As a junior, he started at [[running back]], collecting 158 [[football carry|carries]] for 968 yards (6.1-yard avg.), 13 rushing [[touchdowns]], 17 [[football catch|receptions]] for 246 yards (14.5-yard avg.) and 3 receiving touchdowns. As a senior, he started at safety and contributed to the team winning the 2014 Division I state championship. He tallied 153 [[tackle move|tackles]] (2 for loss), 6 [[interceptions]] (3 returned for touchdowns), 11 passes defensed, 47 carries for 241 yards (5.1-yard avg.), 6 rushing touchdowns, 10 receptions for 148 yards (14.8 avg.) and 3 receiving touchdowns. He received All-Ohio and Cleveland.com All-Star honors. He also practiced [[basketball]] and [[track & field|track]]. ==College career== Dowell accepted a football scholarship from [[Michigan State University]] (MSU). As a true freshman, he played 13 games mainly on [[special teams]], leading the team with 10 tackles. As a sophomore, he made eight-of-12 starts at [[linebacker]], posting 67 tackles and 7 special teams tackles (second on the team). As a junior, he started all 13 games at linebacker, making 74 tackles (second on the team), 2.5 tackles for loss, one sack, 4 passes defensed, one forced [[fumble]] and one fumble recovery. '''Andrew Booth Jr.''' (born September 28, 2000) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[cornerback]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Clemson Tigers football|Clemson Tigers]] and was selected by the [[Minnesota Vikings]] in the second round of the [[2022 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Booth Jr. attended [[Archer High School]] in [[Lawrenceville, Georgia]]. As a junior, he received all-county, all-region and all-state honors.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hammock |first=Will |date=August 6, 2018 |title=SUPER SIX FOOTBALL: Archer senior, Clemson commit Andrew Booth grows into one of nation's best DBs |url=https://www.gwinnettprepsports.com/sports/super-six-football-archer-senior-clemson-commit-andrew-booth-grows-into-one-of-nation-s/article_2e6c8c8c-4f18-5768-9cb7-b08163433cd5.html |access-date=February 18, 2023 |website=Gwinnett Prep Sports |language=en}}</ref>

As a senior, he received all-state, county defensive back of the year and region specialist of the year honors. He played in the 2019 [[Under Armour All-America Game]]. A five-star recruit, he committed to [[Clemson University]] to play [[college football]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Louis-Jacques |first=Marcel |date=July 30, 2018 |title=Five-star cornerback Andrew Booth commits to Clemson |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2018/andrew-booth-clemson-football-recruiting |access-date=February 18, 2023 |website=USA TODAY High School Sports |language=en-US}}</ref>

He was a three-year starter, finishing with 162 tackles, 13 [[interceptions]], 44 passes defensed, 4 forced fumbles, 22 receptions for 557 yards, 4 touchdowns, 3 punt return touchdowns and one blocked field goal.

==College career==
Booth Jr. appeared in 13 games as a true freshman in 2019, collecting 6 tackles and one pass defensed.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Senkiw |first=Brad |date=August 13, 2020 |title=Booth Turning Heads in Fall Camp |url=https://www.si.com/college/clemson/football/clemson-db-andrew-booth-turning-heads-in-fall-camp |access-date=February 18, 2023 |magazine=Sports Illustrated}}</ref>

As a sophomore in 2020, he started four out of 11 games, recording  30 tackles, two interceptions, 4 passes defensed, one [[Quarterback sack|sack]] and a fumble recovery for a 21-yard touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 19, 2021 |title=Clemson's secondary waits to see which Andrew Booth Jr. takes field |url=https://www.goupstate.com/story/sports/2021/07/19/clemson-football-news-roster-secondary-andrew-booth-jr-cornerback-defense-safety/5044566001/ |access-date=February 18, 2023 |website=Go UpState}}</ref> He received ACC Defensive Back of the Week honors, after making 3 tackles, 2 passes defensed and a highlight-reel one-handed interception against the [[University of Virginia]]. He had 7 tackles (one for loss) and his first career sack against [[Georgia Tech]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Needelman |first=Joshua |date=December 17, 2020 |title=Clemson's Booth has rewritten his story since throwing 'The Punch' seen around the nation |url=https://www.postandcourier.com/sports/clemson/clemsons-booth-has-rewritten-his-story-since-throwing-the-punch-seen-around-the-nation/article_6f1b69ea-3efa-11eb-937c-bbd3f67e176b.html |access-date=February 18, 2023 |website=Post and Courier |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Shanesy |first=Todd |date=April 9, 2021 |title=Clemson defensive back is human highlight with need of editing for final cut |url=https://www.greenvilleonline.com/story/sports/2021/04/09/clemson-footballs-andrew-booth-human-highlight-needs-editing/7139049002/ |access-date=February 18, 2023 |website=The Greenville News |language=en-US}}</ref>

As a junior in 2021, he started all 11 games, compiling 39 tackles (3 for loss), 3 interceptions (led the team) and 5 passes defensed. He had 9 tackles (one for loss) against [[Boston College]]. He had 2 interceptions and one pass defensed against the [[University of South Carolina]]. On January 9, 2022, Booth declared for the [[2022 NFL draft]], forgoing his senior season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Whiteman |first=Marc |date=January 10, 2022 |title=Clemson CB Andrew Booth declares for NFL Draft |url=https://www.wyff4.com/article/clemson-cb-andrew-booth-declares-for-nfl-draft/38705675 |access-date=February 18, 2023 |website=WYFF4}}</ref>

===Minnesota Vikings===
Booth was selected by the [[Minnesota Vikings]] in the second round with the 42nd overall pick in the 2022 NFL draft.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Eric |date=April 29, 2022 |title=Vikings Draft Clemson Cornerback Andrew Booth, Jr., with 42nd Overall Pick |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/andrew-booth-jr-nfl-draft-cornerback-clemson |access-date=February 18, 2023 |website=Vikings.com}}</ref> He appeared in 6 games with one start, totaling 12 tackles. He was declared inactive Weeks 2 to 4 with a quad injury. He started in the Week 11 against the [[Dallas Cowboys]] and had a game-high 9 tackles. On November 30, 2022, he was placed on the [[injured reserve list]] with a knee injury.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Alper |first=Josh |date=November 29, 2022 |title=Report: Andrew Booth out for year after having knee surgery |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2022/11/29/report-andrew-booth-out-for-year-after-having-knee-surgery|access-date=February 18, 2023 |website=ProFootballTalk}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=November 30, 2022 |title=Andrew Booth Jr. Placed on IR; Ben Ellefson Activated |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/andrew-booth-ir-injured-reserve-roster-moves|access-date=February 18, 2023 |website=Vikings.com}}</ref>

In 2023, he appeared in 17 games with one start, tallying eight tackles and one pass defensed. He started in the season-finale against the [[Detroit Lions]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andrew Booth 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BootAn00/gamelog/2023/ |access-date=2024-11-28 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

===Dallas Cowboys===
On August 9, 2024, Booth was traded to the [[Dallas Cowboys]] in exchange for [[Nahshon Wright]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Shook |first1=Nick |title=Cowboys send CB Nahshon Wright to Vikings in exchange for CB Andrew Booth |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/cowboys-send-cb-nahshon-wright-to-vikings-in-exchange-for-cb-andrew-booth |website=NFL |date=August 9, 2024 |access-date=August 10, 2024}}</ref> He was released on November 5 and was signed to the [[practice squad]] two days later.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dallas Cowboys bring back Andrew Booth, add cornerback to practice squad |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/cowboys/2024/11/07/dallas-cowboys-bring-back-andrew-booth-add-cornerback-to-practice-squad/ |website=The Dallas Morning News|date=November 7, 2024|access-date=November 7, 2024}}</ref> Booth was promoted to the active roster on December 21.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Williams |first=Charean |author-link=Charean Williams |date=2024-12-21 |title=Cowboys place CB Trevon Diggs on IR, sign CB Andrew Booth to active roster |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/cowboys-place-cb-trevon-diggs-on-ir-sign-cb-andrew-booth-to-active-roster |access-date=2024-12-27 |website=NBC Sports}}</ref> On August 27, 2025, he was released by the Cowboys.<ref>{{cite web|title=Cowboys roster move: Andrew Booth, Zion Childress released|url=https://www.bloggingtheboys.com/dallas-cowboys-roster/179040/andrew-booth-zion-childress-released-practice-squad|work=Blogging the Boys|date=August 27, 2025}}</ref>

=== Louisville Kings ===
On January 14, 2026, Booth was selected by the [[Louisville Kings]] of the [[United Football League (2024)|United Football League]] (UFL).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Day Two of UFL Draft Introduces New Faces and Ignites the New Era of Spring Football |url=https://www.theufl.com/news/day-two-of-ufl-draft-introduces-new-faces-and-ignites-the-new-era-of-spring-football |access-date=2026-01-16 |website=www.theufl.com |language=en}}</ref>

'''Andrei Iosivas''' (born October 15, 1999; {{ipac-en|'|j|oʊ|s|i|ˌ|v|ɑː|ʃ}} {{respell|YOH|Shee|VAHSH}}<ref>{{cite AV media|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CF9Jwg36N4w |title=Andrei Iosivas Hopes Journey From Hawaii to Princeton Leads to NFL |publisher=[[NBC10 Philadelphia]] |via=YouTube |date=April 25, 2023 |accessdate=May 3, 2023 |time=0:07}}</ref>) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[wide receiver]] for the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Princeton Tigers football|Princeton Tigers]] and was selected by the Bengals in the sixth round of the [[2023 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Iosivas was born on October 15, 1999, in [[Tokyo]], Japan, to a [[Filipinos|Filipino]] mother and [[Romanians|Romanian]] father.<ref>{{cite web | last=Sheeran | first=John | title=Bengals rookie says Cincinnati 'felt like home' during draft visit | website=atozsports.com | date=2023-05-09 | url=https://atozsports.com/nfl/cincinnati-bengals-news/bengals-andrei-iosivas-speaks-on-being-a-perfect-fit-in-star-studded-offense/ | access-date=2024-07-19}}</ref><ref name="j679">{{cite web | last=Hobson | first=Geoff | title=Bengals Rookie WR Andrei Iosivas Finds His Route And It's A Go | website=The Official Site of the Cincinnati Bengals | date=2023-08-26 | url=https://www.bengals.com/news/andrei-iosivas-finds-his-path | access-date=2024-07-19}}</ref> He has one younger brother. When he was 4, his family moved to [[Honolulu]], Hawaii, where he attended [[Punahou School]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hobson |first=Geoff |date=August 26, 2023 |title=Bengals Rookie WR Andrei Iosivas Finds His Route And It's A Go |url=https://www.bengals.com/news/andrei-iosivas-finds-his-path |access-date=October 16, 2025 |website=Cincinnati Bengals}}</ref><ref name="g439">{{Cite web |last=Abramo |first=Nick |date=2018-05-13 |title=Iosivas leads Punahou boys to state track title |url=https://www.staradvertiser.com/2018/05/13/sports/iosivas-leads-punahou-boys-to-state-track-title/ |access-date=2024-07-19 |website=[[Honolulu Star-Advertiser]]}}</ref> He became an [[Americans|American]] citizen when he was 17.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.essentiallysports.com/nfl-active-news-is-andrei-iosivas-filipino-ethnicity-nationality-more-about-the-bengals-wr/|title=Is Andrei Iosivas Filipino? Iosivas was selected by the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] in the sixth round, 206th overall, of the [[2023 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cleveland.com/bengals/2023/04/bengals-select-wide-receiver-andrei-iosivas-with-206th-pick-in-2023-nfl-draft.html|title=Bengals select wide receiver Andrei Iosivas with 206th pick in 2023 NFL Draft|first=Andrew|last=Gillis|website=[[Cleveland.com]]|date=April 29, 2023|access-date=April 30, 2023}}</ref>

He made his first career reception, a 9-yard contested sideline catch, in the Bengals' Week 5 game against the [[Arizona Cardinals]].<ref>{{Cite tweet |number=1711146744413896979|user=pauldehnerjr |title=First career catch for Andrei Iosivas. |date=October 8, 2023}}</ref> In Week 6 against the [[Seattle Seahawks]], Iosivas scored his first career touchdown on a 3-yard pass from quarterback [[Joe Burrow]] in a game the Bengals won 17–13.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rapien |first=James |date=October 15, 2023 |title=Watch: Bengals Rookie Andrei Iosivas Scores First Touchdown of NFL Career |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/bengals/gameday/watch-bengals-rookie-andrei-iosivas-scores-first-touchdown-of-nfl-career |access-date=October 15, 2023 |website=Sports Illustrated |language=en}}</ref> Iosivas grabbed his second career touchdown on a 2-yard pass against the [[San Francisco 49ers]] in what ended up being his only target of the game.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Heltman |first=Russ |date=October 29, 2023 |title=Watch: Andrei Iosivas Caps Off Historic Bengals Quarter With Touchdown |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/bengals/gameday/watch-andrei-iosivas-caps-off-historic-bengals-quarter-with-touchdown |access-date=October 30, 2023 |website=Sports Illustrated |language=en}}</ref> Iosivas missed the Bengals' Week 11 contest against the [[Baltimore Ravens]] due to a knee injury.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 15, 2023 |title=Bengals' Andrei Iosivas: Won't play Thursday |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/bengals-andrei-iosivas-wont-play-thursday/ |access-date=November 15, 2023 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}}</ref>

In Week 18 against the Cleveland Browns, Iosivas played his first career game as a starter, due to [[Tee Higgins]] re-aggravating a hamstring injury. Iosivas had a solid game, with five receptions on seven targets for 36 yards and two touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Heltman |first=Russ |date=January 7, 2024 |title=Watch: Jake Browning Connects With Andrei Iosivas For Second Touchdown of Game Against Browns |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/bengals/gameday/watch-jake-browning-connects-with-andrei-iosivas-for-second-touchdown-of-game-against-browns |access-date=January 10, 2024 |website=Sports Illustrated |language=en}}</ref> He finished his rookie season with 15 receptions, 116 yards, and four touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andrei Iosivas 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/I/IosiAn00/gamelog/2023/ |access-date=2024-07-19 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

=== 2024 ===
Iosivas was named the Bengals starting third wide receiver after the departure of [[Tyler Boyd (American football)|Tyler Boyd]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Garrison |first=Drew |date=2024-09-03 |title=Bengals release Week 1 depth chart |url=https://www.cincyjungle.com/2024/9/3/24234950/bengals-depth-chart-vs-patriots-nfl-week-1 |access-date=2024-09-16 |website=Cincy Jungle |language=en}}</ref> He recorded a two-touchdown game during the Bengals' Week 2 loss to the [[2024 Kansas City Chiefs season|Kansas City Chiefs]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Clark |first=Dave |date=September 15, 2024 |title=CBS' Jim Nantz on Andrei Iosivas: 'You'll be saying that (name) a lot in years to come' |url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/nfl/bengals/2024/09/15/cbs-jim-nantz-tony-romo-praise-bengals-andrei-iosivas-vs-chiefs-nfl-week-2/75239961007/ |access-date=2024-09-16 |website=The Enquirer |language=en-US}}</ref> He finished the 2024 season with 36 receptions for 479 yards and six touchdowns.
<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andrei Iosivas 2024 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/I/IosiAn00/gamelog/2024/ |access-date=2025-04-12 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

=== 2025 ===
Iosivas maintained his role as the third wide receiver for the Bengals.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rapien |first=James |date=June 6, 2025 |title=Bengals Star Believes Team Uncovered Under The Radar Weapon on Offense |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/bengals/onsi/news/tee-higgins-believes-third-year-wide-receiver-andrei-iosivas-could-be-under-radar-weapon-bengals-2025-01jwvnm3asgb |access-date=March 2, 2026 |website=Cincinnati Bengals On SI |language=en-US}}</ref>  On October 5, Iosivas had 5 receptions for a career high 82 yards in a 37-24 loss to the Detroit Lions.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Morrison |first=Jay |date=October 7, 2025 |title=Bengals WR Andrei Iosvias' Career Game - and New Wrinkle - Offers Sign of Life for Struggling Offense |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/bengals/onsi/bengals-wr-andrei-iosvias-career-game-and-new-wrinkle-offers-sign-of-life-for-struggling-offense-01k6zjrtq5vq |access-date=March 2, 2026 |website=Cincinnati Bengals On SI |language=en-US}}</ref>

==College career==
Farmer attended and played college football at Lane College.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andrew Farmer - Football |url=https://golcdragons.com/sports/football/roster/andrew-farmer/2086 |access-date=November 18, 2023 |website=Lane College Athletics |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Jones |first=Zach |date=August 31, 2023 |title=Former Lane College football player Andrew Farmer II makes Los Angeles Chargers |url=https://www.wbbjtv.com/2023/08/30/former-lane-college-football-player-andrew-farmer-ii-makes-los-angeles-chargers/ |access-date=November 18, 2023 |website=WBBJ TV |language=en-US}}</ref> In Farmer's college career, he notched 140 tackles and 19.5 sacks.<ref>{{cite web |title=Andrew Farmer Stats |url=https://www.footballdb.com/players/andrew-farmer-farmean01 |website=Football Database |access-date=October 2, 2023}}</ref>

=== Los Angeles Chargers ===
Farmer signed as an undrafted free agent with the [[Los Angeles Chargers]]. He was waived following final roster cuts on August 29, 2023 and subsequently signed to the [[practice squad]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Reed |first=Jason |date=April 29, 2023 |title=Chargers roster cuts tracker: Official 53-man roster announced (update) |url=https://boltbeat.com/posts/chargers-roster-cuts-tracker-2023 |access-date=22 November 2023 |website=Bolt Beat|publisher=Fansided}}</ref> He made his NFL debut in Week 4 against the Las Vegas Raiders. On November 22, Farmer was signed to the active roster following an injury to [[Joey Bosa]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Alper |first=Josh |date=November 22, 2023 |title=With Joey Bosa going on IR, Chargers will promote Andrew Farmer II |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/with-joey-bosa-going-on-ir-chargers-will-promote-andrew-farmer-ii |access-date=22 November 2023 |website=NBC Sports}}</ref>

On August 27, 2024, Farmer was waived by the Chargers and re-signed to the practice squad, but released a few days later.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 27, 2024 |title=Los Angeles Chargers Reduce Roster to 53 Players |url=https://www.chargers.com/news/los-angeles-chargers-reduce-roster-to-53-players-2024 |access-date=2024-09-02 |website=Chargers.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=August 28, 2024 |title=Chargers Claim Hassan Haskins; Sign 15 Players to Practice Squad |url=https://www.chargers.com/news/claim-hassan-haskins-sign-15-players-to-practice-squad-2024 |access-date=2024-09-02 |website=Chargers.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite tweet|title=we’ve signed CB Shaun Wade and WR Dez Fitzpatrick to our practice squad and released WR Cornelius Johnson and OLB Andrew Farmer II.|user=Chargers|number=1830727425438982639}}</ref>

=== Denver Broncos ===
On September 17, 2024, Farmer was signed to the [[Denver Broncos]]' practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kelberman |first=Zack |date=2024-09-17 |title=Report: Broncos Sign OLB After Browning Injury |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/broncos/news/broncos-sign-andrew-farmer-browning-injury |access-date=2024-09-19 |website=Sports Illustrated |language=en-US}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract with Denver on January 13, 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |last=DiLalla |first=Aric |date=January 13, 2025 |title=Broncos sign 13 players to future contracts |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-sign-13-players-to-future-contracts |access-date=2025-07-03 |website=DenverBroncos.com}}</ref> On August 25, Farmer was waived by the Broncos.<ref>{{cite web |last1=DiLalla |first1=Aric |title=Broncos make series of roster moves ahead of 53-man roster deadline |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-make-series-of-roster-moves-ahead-of-53-man-roster-deadline |website=denverbroncos.com |access-date=26 August 2025}}</ref>

===San Francisco 49ers===
On November 5, 2025, Farmer signed with the [[San Francisco 49ers]]' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=49ers Sign Defensive Lineman, Release Linebacker|url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-sign-defensive-lineman-release-linebacker|website=49ers.com|date=November 5, 2025}}</ref> On January 20, 2026, he signed a reserve/futures contract with San Francisco.<ref>{{cite web |title=49ers Sign 14 Players to Reserve/Future Contracts |url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-sign-14-players-to-reserve-future-contracts |website=49ers.com |access-date=21 January 2026}}</ref>

Coker signed with the [[Las Vegas Raiders]] as an undrafted free agent on April 27, 2024.<ref>{{cite web|title=Raiders announce undrafted free agents|url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-undrafted-free-agents-nfl-2024-rookies|website=Raiders.com|date=April 27, 2024}}</ref> He was also selected by the [[Birmingham Stallions (2022)|Birmingham Stallions]] in the seventh round of the [[2024 UFL draft]] on July 17.<ref>{{cite news |title=2024 UFL College Draft: Showboats select Kansas QB Jason Bean with No. 1 pick |url=https://www.foxsports.com/stories/ufl/2024-ufl-college-draft-tracking-every-selection |website=FoxSports.com |date=July 17, 2024 |access-date=July 19, 2024}}</ref> He was waived on August 27.<ref>{{cite web|title=Raiders make moves to bring roster to 53-player limit|url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-make-moves-to-bring-roster-to-53-man-roster-nfl-2024-transactions|website=Raiders.com|date=August 27, 2024}}</ref>

===Cincinnati Bengals===
On October 22, 2024, Coker was signed to the [[Cincinnati Bengals]]' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=OT Andrew Coker signed; DT Domenique Davis waived|url=https://www.bengals.com/news/ot-andrew-coker-signed-dt-domenique-davis-waived-bengals-roster-update|website=Bengals.com|date=October 22, 2024}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract with the Bengals on January 7, 2025.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bengals Sign 11 Players to Reserve/Future Contracts|url=https://www.bengals.com/news/bengals-sign-11-players-to-reserve-future-contracts-bengals-roster-update|website=Bengals.com|date=January 7, 2025}}</ref>

On August 26, 2025, Coker was waived by the Bengals as part of final roster cuts and re-signed to the practice squad the next day.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bengals Reduce Final Roster to 53 Players for 2025 Season |url=https://www.bengals.com/news/bengals-reduce-final-roster-53-2025-season |website=Bengals.com |access-date=27 August 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Bengals Sign 14 Players to 2025 Practice Squad BENGALS ROSTER UPDATE |url=https://www.bengals.com/news/bengals-set-initial-2025-practice-squad |website=Bengals.com |access-date=28 August 2025}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract with Cincinnati on January 5, 2026.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bengals Sign 13 Players to Reserve/Future Contracts, Six Players to Contract Extensions {{!}} BENGALS ROSTER UPDATE|url=https://www.bengals.com/news/bengals-reserve-future-contracts-extensions-2026-roster-update|website=Bengals.com|date=January 5, 2026}}</ref>
