[[LSU Tigers football|LSU]] (2023) | undraftedyear = 2024 | pastteams = * [[Philadelphia Eagles]] ({{NFL Year|2024}}–present) | status = Active | highlights = * [[List of Super Bowl champions|Super Bowl champion]] ([[Super Bowl LIX|LIX]]) | statseason = | statweek = | statlabel1 = | statvalue1 = | statlabel2 = | statvalue2 = | pfr = SamxAn00 }} '''Andre' Sam''' (born February 9, 1999) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] for the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[McNeese Cowboys football|McNeese Cowboys]], [[Marshall Thundering Herd football|Marshall Thundering Herd]] and [[LSU Tigers football|LSU Tigers]]. ==Early life== Sam was born on February 9, 1999, and grew up in [[Iowa, Louisiana]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.foxsports.com/nfl/andre-sam-player-bio|publisher=[[Fox Sports]]|title=Andre' Sam}} He has a [[speech disorder]] that causes him to [[Stuttering|stutter]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.nola.com/sports/lsu/how-lsu-db-andre-sam-came-from-fcs-walk-on-and-found-himself/article_2f3b716a-fab1-11ed-8784-235cc335eda9.html|website=[[Nola.com]]|title=4 teams, 7 years: André Sam took a modern journey to LSU — and found himself on the way|date=May 25, 2023|author=Alexander, Wilson}} He was raised by his mother after his father and grandfather died when he was age six.{{Cite news|url=https://www.pennlive.com/philadelphiaeagles/2024/11/eagles-rookie-honors-late-brother-by-making-nfl-i-let-him-live-inside-of-me.html|newspaper=[[The Patriot-News]]|title=Eagles rookie uses brother's death to inspire NFL dreams: 'We both play' for Philadelphia|author=Steele, Cayden|date=November 21, 2024}} Growing up, he trained in [[American football|football]] with his older brother, Aaron, who went on to play [[college football]] for the [[McNeese Cowboys football|McNeese Cowboys]]. Sam attended [[Iowa High School]] where he played football, being an all-state [[wide receiver]] and [[Return specialist|kick returner]], and participated in [[track and field]], being a district [[long jump]] champion and district champion in two relay events.{{Cite web|url=https://lsusports.net/sports/fb/roster/player/andre-sam/|publisher=[[LSU Tigers]]|title=Andre' Sam}} However, at the start of his [[Senior (education)|senior]] year, his brother Aaron was killed in a shooting, and Sam considered quitting the sport. Sam opted to continue to play and had 775 receiving yards and 11 receiving [[touchdown]]s that year, helping Iowa reach the state playoff quarterfinals. Due to his weight, {{convert|150|lb}}, and his status as a small school prospect, Sam received no offers to play college football and [[Walk-on (sports)|walked-on]] to the local [[McNeese Cowboys football|McNeese Cowboys]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.cbslakecharles.tv/2024/01/11/478156/living-dream-for-two|publisher=[[KSWL-LD]]|title=Living Dream for Two |date=January 11, 2024|author=Swire, Kelsey}} ==College career== Sam became a [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] and [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]] as a true [[freshman]] at McNeese in 2017. He wore the number 21, previously worn by his brother, during the 2018 season, but only appeared in three games, posting six [[Tackle (football move)|tackles]], before suffering a torn labrum. He saw more playing time in 2019, playing 12 games and recording 51 tackles, seven [[Pass deflected|pass breakups]] and an [[interception]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.kplctv.com/2024/01/06/former-iowa-safety-andre-sam-declares-2024-nfl-draft/|publisher=[[KPLC]]|title=Former Iowa Safety Andre Sam Declares for 2024 NFL Draft|author=Travis, Matthew|date=January 5, 2024}} The 2020 season was postponed to spring 2021 due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], and he then appeared in all seven games during the spring 2021 season while leading the team with 52 tackles and three interceptions. He was a first-team All-[[Southland Conference]] (SLC) selection for the spring 2021 season.{{Cite web|url=https://www.nola.com/sports/lsu/lsu-football-adds-former-marshall-transfer-safety-andr-sam/article_d420cb58-f59d-11ed-bf40-738d198b14be.html|website=[[Nola.com]]|title=LSU adds to the secondary with seventh-year transfer safety from state of Louisiana|date=May 18, 2023|author=Alexander, Wilson}} In the fall 2021 season, he placed second in the team with 70 tackles and made a team-leading seven pass breakups along with one interception, repeating as a first-team All-SLC pick.{{Cite web|url=https://www.kplctv.com/2021/12/02/mcneese-all-conference-safety-andr-sam-enters-transfer-portal/|publisher=[[KPLC]]|title=McNeese all-conference safety André Sam enters the transfer portal|date=December 2, 2021|author=Renard, Brady}} Sam graduated from McNeese following the 2021 season but opted to continue his college football career, having received extra eligibility due to the COVID-19 pandemic and a medical redshirt from his injured 2018 season. He entered the [[NCAA transfer portal]] and concluded his stint at McNeese having appeared in 33 games while posting 179 tackles, 19 passes defended and five interceptions. Television station [[KSWL-LD]] noted that in his tenure with the team, Sam "had to play through three head coaches and deal with a pair of hurricanes that wiped out almost all of the Cowboy facilities." He ended up transferring to the [[Marshall Thundering Herd football|Marshall Thundering Herd]] for the 2022 season.{{Cite web|url=https://www.kplctv.com/2021/12/16/mcneese-transfer-safety-andr-sam-signs-with-marshall/|publisher=[[KPLC]]|title=McNeese transfer safety André Sam signs with Marshall|date=December 16, 2021|author=Renard, Brady}} With Marshall in the 2022 season, Sam totaled 53 tackles, 5.5 tackles-for-loss (TFLs) and seven pass breakups, being named honorable mention All-[[Sun Belt Conference]] (SBC). He opted to transfer again, and committed to the [[LSU Tigers football|LSU Tigers]] for the 2023 season – his seventh and final year of college football. He was granted a medical waiver by the [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]] to be able to play in 2023. With the Tigers, he finished with 85 tackles and a team-leading three interceptions, earning the team's Defensive Player of the Year award.{{Cite web|url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-sign-ej-jenkins-to-the-active-roster-place-dallas-goedert-on-injured-reserve|publisher=[[Philadelphia Eagles]]|title=Eagles sign TE E.J. Jenkins to the active roster, place TE Dallas Goedert on Injured Reserve |author=McPherson, Chris|date=December 7, 2024}} Across his time with McNeese, Marshall and LSU, Sam played in 68 games, 61 as a starter, making 317 tackles 11 TFLs and nine interceptions. He was invited to the 2024 [[NFL Scouting Combine]].{{Cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/lsu/article/2024-nfl-scouting-combine-lsu-tigers-andre-sam-tracker-friday-227950595/|website=[[247Sports]]|title=Tracking the LSU Tigers at NFL Combine on Friday|author=Shipp, Sonny|date=March 1, 2024}} ==Professional career== {{NFL predraft | height ft = 5 | height in = 10 7/8 | weight = 191 | dash = 4.53 | ten split = 1.67 | twenty split = 2.60 | shuttle = 4.32 | cone drill = 7.03 | vertical = 36.0 | broad ft = 10 | broad in = 3 | bench = 14 | arm span = 30 | hand span = 9 1/4 | wingspan ft = 6 | wingspan in = 1 3/8 | note = All values from [[NFL Combine]]/[[Pro Day]]{{Cite web |url=https://www.nfl.com/prospects/andre-sam/32005341-4d00-0469-48d8-b13e0a0e9cf3 |title=Andre' Sam Draft and Combine Prospect Profile |website=NFL.com |access-date=February 1, 2025}}{{Cite web |url=https://draftscout.com/dsprofile.php?PlayerId=1056472&DraftYear=2024 |title=Andre' Sam College Football Profile |website=DraftScout.com |access-date=February 1, 2025}} }} After going unselected in the [[2024 NFL draft]], Sam signed with the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] as an [[Free agent#Undrafted free agent|undrafted free agent]].
